# Missing Vendor API Bindings

Short-lived audit/task document for tracking gaps between upstream native
library API surfaces and Stark's bundled `Vendor.*` bindings. Delete this file
when the gaps have either been implemented or moved into the normal roadmap.

Audit rule: for each Vendor binding, use the latest stable upstream API surface
as the source of truth, list what Stark currently exposes, and document every
missing upstream entry point. Stable public APIs become implementation tasks.
Deprecated, obsolete, private, or static-linking-only APIs are documented
separately and should not become first-class Stark APIs unless a compatibility
need is explicit.

## Audit Status

| Binding | Upstream surface audited | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Vendor.LZ4` | LZ4 `v1.10.0` `lz4.h`, `lz4hc.h`, `lz4frame.h` | Incomplete; simple block API only |
| `Vendor.Zlib` | zlib `v1.3.2` `zlib.h`, `zconf.h` | Incomplete; one-shot zlib blocks and basic zlib streaming only |
| `Vendor.Curl` | curl/libcurl `8.20.0` public headers and function index | Incomplete; two HTTP GET helpers only |
| `Vendor.STB.Image` | STB snapshot `31c1ad37456438565541f4919958214b6e762fb4`: `stb_image.h` v2.30, `stb_image_write.h` v1.16, `stb_image_resize2.h` v2.18 | Incomplete; 8-bit load, PNG/BMP/TGA file write, and one packed uint8 linear resize path only |
| `Vendor.STB.Truetype` | STB snapshot `31c1ad37456438565541f4919958214b6e762fb4`: `stb_truetype.h` v1.26 | Incomplete; safe owned-font wrapper covers basic glyph lookup, metrics, bitmap render, and one-shot range packing only |
| `Vendor.Miniaudio` | miniaudio `0.11.25` `miniaudio.h` | Incomplete; safe decode/playback helper only, with encoding/generation/resource-manager/node-graph/engine disabled in the native build |
| `Vendor.Cgltf` | cgltf `v1.15` `cgltf.h`, plus upstream-but-not-vendored `cgltf_write.h` | Incomplete; safe asset-summary wrapper only, no raw data graph, accessor payload reads, transform helpers, extensions/extras, custom options, or writer API |
| `Vendor.GLFW` | GLFW `3.4` `GLFW/glfw3.h`, `GLFW/glfw3native.h` | Incomplete; minimal window/context/input/Vulkan helper only, no monitors, cursors, clipboard, joystick/gamepad, gamma, full window attributes, full callbacks, native access, init/platform options, or complete constants |
| `Vendor.KbTextShape` | HarfBuzz `14.2.1` public headers plus ICU `78.3` `ubrk.h` / `utext.h` | Incomplete; narrow segmentation and glyph-shaping convenience wrapper only, no full HarfBuzz buffer/font/feature/OpenType/subset/color/draw APIs and no full ICU BreakIterator/UText surface |
| `Vendor.SQLite` | SQLite `3.53.2` official C interface, `sqlite3.h`, and `sqlite3ext.h` | Incomplete; safe open/prepare/step/basic bind/basic column wrapper only, no blob I/O, backup, hooks, custom functions, collations, virtual tables, VFS, serialization, status/config, extension API, or complete constants |
| `Vendor.SDL3` | SDL `3.4.10` public symbol index and local `SDL3/SDL*.h` headers | Incomplete; init/window/renderer/event/audio-stream convenience wrapper only, no complete raw SDL3 surface, GPU, surfaces/textures, input devices, filesystem/storage, threading/sync, properties, dialogs, clipboard, platform, Vulkan/OpenGL/EGL/Metal, or complete constants/types |
| `Vendor.Raylib` | Raylib `6.0` `raylib.h`, `raymath.h`, and `rlgl.h` | Incomplete; core functions, structs, enum values, `raymath`, and safe `rlgl` wrappers are covered; remaining gaps are weak callback aliases, no strong enum types, legacy unsafe/raw public surfaces, incomplete safe ownership wrappers, and UTF-8/text policy |
| `Vendor.Vulkan` | Vulkan-Headers `v1.4.354` registry `vk.xml` and `vulkan_core.h` | Incomplete; local registry is pinned to header `350` while latest is `354`, only 45/857 commands are internal raw FFI, no public raw `vk*` surface, most ABI carriers/constants are missing, and the package is currently a bootstrap/triangle helper rather than a complete Vulkan binding |

## `Vendor.LZ4`

### Source Of Truth

Audited against latest stable upstream LZ4 release `v1.10.0`, published July
22, 2024:

- <https://github.com/lz4/lz4/releases/tag/v1.10.0>
- <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lz4/lz4/v1.10.0/lib/lz4.h>
- <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lz4/lz4/v1.10.0/lib/lz4hc.h>
- <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lz4/lz4/v1.10.0/lib/lz4frame.h>

### Current Stark Coverage

Current file: `vendor/src/Vendor/LZ4.stark`.

Stark currently exposes:

- `LZ4MaxInputSize`
- `LZ4MaxBlockSize`
- `LZ4Error`
- `LZ4BlockResult`
- `VersionNumber()`
- `MaxCompressedSize(sourceLength)`
- `CompressBlock(source, destination)`
- `DecompressBlock(compressed, destination)`
- `DecompressBlockPrefix(compressed, compressedLength, destination)`

Current internal native symbols:

- `LZ4_versionNumber`
- `LZ4_compressBound`
- `LZ4_compress_default`
- `LZ4_decompress_safe`

Assessment: `Vendor.LZ4` is incomplete. It wraps the safest simple block
compression/decompression path only. It does not expose acceleration tuning,
external state compression, destination-size compression, partial
decompression, dictionary compression/decompression, streaming block APIs,
high-compression APIs, or LZ4 frame APIs.

### Missing Stable Block API From `lz4.h`

- `LZ4_versionString`: return the native library version string.
- `LZ4_compress_fast`: simple block compression with acceleration tradeoff.
- `LZ4_sizeofState`: required byte count for caller-owned compression state.
- `LZ4_compress_fast_extState`: block compression using caller-owned state.
- `LZ4_compress_destSize`: fill a destination budget while reporting consumed input bytes.
- `LZ4_decompress_safe_partial`: decode only the requested prefix of a compressed block.
- `LZ4_createStream`: allocate streaming compression state.
- `LZ4_freeStream`: free streaming compression state.
- `LZ4_resetStream_fast`: reset a known-valid compression stream cheaply.
- `LZ4_loadDict`: load a dictionary into a compression stream.
- `LZ4_loadDictSlow`: load a dictionary with more expensive/better indexing.
- `LZ4_attach_dictionary`: attach a preloaded dictionary stream to a working stream.
- `LZ4_compress_fast_continue`: streaming block compression over dependent blocks.
- `LZ4_saveDict`: save trailing dictionary bytes when the prior source region cannot stay fixed.
- `LZ4_createStreamDecode`: allocate streaming decompression state.
- `LZ4_freeStreamDecode`: free streaming decompression state.
- `LZ4_setStreamDecode`: reset/configure streaming decompression with optional dictionary.
- `LZ4_decoderRingBufferSize`: compute ring-buffer size for streaming decompression.
- `LZ4_decompress_safe_continue`: streaming block decompression over dependent blocks.
- `LZ4_decompress_safe_usingDict`: stateless block decompression with external dictionary.
- `LZ4_decompress_safe_partial_usingDict`: partial block decompression with external dictionary.
- `LZ4_initStream`: initialize caller-owned compression state storage.
- `LZ4_resetStream`: older reset entry point; still exported, but upstream says callers should consider `LZ4_initStream` because future versions may warn.

Missing public constants/macros/type facts that should be represented as Stark
constants or safe helper APIs:

- `LZ4_VERSION_MAJOR`
- `LZ4_VERSION_MINOR`
- `LZ4_VERSION_RELEASE`
- `LZ4_VERSION_NUMBER`
- `LZ4_VERSION_STRING`
- `LZ4_MEMORY_USAGE_MIN`
- `LZ4_MEMORY_USAGE_DEFAULT`
- `LZ4_MEMORY_USAGE_MAX`
- `LZ4_MAX_INPUT_SIZE`
- `LZ4_COMPRESSBOUND(isize)` as a comptime-capable Stark helper if practical
- `LZ4_DECODER_RING_BUFFER_SIZE(maxBlockSize)` as a comptime-capable Stark helper if practical
- opaque handle coverage for `LZ4_stream_t`
- opaque handle coverage for `LZ4_streamDecode_t`

### Missing Stable High-Compression API From `lz4hc.h`

- `LZ4_compress_HC`: one-shot high-compression block compression.
- `LZ4_sizeofStateHC`: required byte count for caller-owned HC state.
- `LZ4_compress_HC_extStateHC`: HC compression using caller-owned state.
- `LZ4_compress_HC_destSize`: HC compression constrained by destination budget while reporting consumed input bytes.
- `LZ4_createStreamHC`: allocate HC streaming compression state.
- `LZ4_freeStreamHC`: free HC streaming compression state.
- `LZ4_resetStreamHC_fast`: cheap reset for a known-valid HC stream.
- `LZ4_loadDictHC`: load a dictionary into an HC stream.
- `LZ4_compress_HC_continue`: HC streaming block compression over dependent blocks.
- `LZ4_compress_HC_continue_destSize`: HC streaming compression constrained by destination budget.
- `LZ4_saveDictHC`: save trailing HC dictionary bytes.
- `LZ4_attach_HC_dictionary`: attach a preloaded HC dictionary stream to a working HC stream.
- `LZ4_initStreamHC`: initialize caller-owned HC stream storage.
- `LZ4_resetStreamHC`: older HC reset entry point; prefer `LZ4_initStreamHC` / `LZ4_resetStreamHC_fast` in new wrappers.

Missing public constants/type facts:

- `LZ4HC_CLEVEL_MIN`
- `LZ4HC_CLEVEL_DEFAULT`
- `LZ4HC_CLEVEL_OPT_MIN`
- `LZ4HC_CLEVEL_MAX`
- opaque handle coverage for `LZ4_streamHC_t`

### Missing Stable Frame API From `lz4frame.h`

Frame APIs are the most important user-facing gap. The `lz4` CLI works with
frames, not raw blocks, and frames carry metadata needed for portable
self-contained compressed data.

- `LZ4F_isError`
- `LZ4F_getErrorName`

### Implementation Tasks

- [ ] Add safe version string support:
  - bind `LZ4_versionString`
  - expose `VersionString()` as borrowed/copied Stark text with correct C string lifetime handling
  - add C# compiler tests and Stark self-hosted tests for the binding shape

- [ ] Add fast block compression:
  - bind `LZ4_compress_fast`
  - expose `CompressBlockFast(source, destination, acceleration)` with a bounded acceleration type
  - preserve current `CompressBlock` as the default/simple path
  - test default-equivalent acceleration and high acceleration output round trips

- [ ] Add external-state block compression:
  - bind `LZ4_sizeofState`, `LZ4_compress_fast_extState`, and `LZ4_initStream`
  - decide between a safe owned `CompressionState` handle and caller-owned scratch-buffer API
  - ensure state storage alignment requirements are represented and checked
  - test repeated calls reuse the same state without allocation

- [ ] Add destination-size block compression:
  - bind `LZ4_compress_destSize`
  - expose an API that returns both produced bytes and consumed source bytes
  - ensure the destination target size is at least one byte before calling native code
  - test partial consumption and exact-fit cases

- [ ] Add partial block decompression:
  - bind `LZ4_decompress_safe_partial`
  - expose `DecompressBlockPrefixToTarget(compressed, destination, targetOutputSize)`
  - reject `targetOutputSize > destination.Length` before FFI
  - test short-prefix decode and malformed input failure

- [ ] Add block dictionary decompression:
  - bind `LZ4_decompress_safe_usingDict`
  - bind `LZ4_decompress_safe_partial_usingDict`
  - expose safe dictionary-slice APIs with dictionary lifetime limited to the call
  - test one-shot dictionary round trips

- [ ] Add streaming compression state:
  - bind `LZ4_createStream`, `LZ4_freeStream`, `LZ4_resetStream_fast`, `LZ4_loadDict`, `LZ4_loadDictSlow`, `LZ4_attach_dictionary`, `LZ4_compress_fast_continue`, and `LZ4_saveDict`
  - expose an owned `CompressionStream` with deterministic `Close`/`drop`
  - represent dictionary attachment without letting the dictionary storage escape or be mutated during use
  - test dependent-block compression and safe dictionary saving

- [ ] Add streaming decompression state:
  - bind `LZ4_createStreamDecode`, `LZ4_freeStreamDecode`, `LZ4_setStreamDecode`, `LZ4_decoderRingBufferSize`, and `LZ4_decompress_safe_continue`
  - expose an owned `DecompressionStream`
  - expose `DecoderRingBufferSize(maxBlockSize)` with bounded `maxBlockSize`
  - test dependent-block decompression with a ring-buffer style destination

- [ ] Add high-compression constants and one-shot HC compression:
  - bind/expose `LZ4HC_CLEVEL_MIN`, `LZ4HC_CLEVEL_DEFAULT`, `LZ4HC_CLEVEL_OPT_MIN`, and `LZ4HC_CLEVEL_MAX`
  - bind `LZ4_compress_HC`
  - expose `CompressBlockHigh(source, destination, level)`
  - test min/default/max level round trips

- [ ] Add high-compression external-state APIs:
  - bind `LZ4_sizeofStateHC`, `LZ4_compress_HC_extStateHC`, and `LZ4_initStreamHC`
  - expose safe HC state storage with alignment checks
  - test repeated HC compression with reused state

- [ ] Add high-compression destination-size APIs:
  - bind `LZ4_compress_HC_destSize`
  - expose produced/consumed counts
  - bind `LZ4_compress_HC_continue_destSize` as part of the streaming HC work
  - test destination-budget behavior

- [ ] Add high-compression streaming state:
  - bind `LZ4_createStreamHC`, `LZ4_freeStreamHC`, `LZ4_resetStreamHC_fast`, `LZ4_loadDictHC`, `LZ4_compress_HC_continue`, `LZ4_saveDictHC`, `LZ4_attach_HC_dictionary`, and `LZ4_resetStreamHC`
  - expose an owned `HighCompressionStream`
  - preserve level selection and dictionary lifetime constraints
  - test dependent-block HC compression and dictionary reuse

- [ ] Add LZ4 frame ABI carriers and constants:
  - define Stark equivalents for `LZ4F_errorCode_t`, `LZ4F_blockSizeID_t`, `LZ4F_blockMode_t`, `LZ4F_contentChecksum_t`, `LZ4F_blockChecksum_t`, `LZ4F_frameType_t`, `LZ4F_frameInfo_t`, `LZ4F_preferences_t`, `LZ4F_compressOptions_t`, and `LZ4F_decompressOptions_t`
  - expose constants for `LZ4F_VERSION`, header/checksum sizes, magic numbers, block sizes, block modes, checksum flags, and frame types
  - provide constructors/default helpers corresponding to `LZ4F_INIT_FRAMEINFO` and `LZ4F_INIT_PREFERENCES`
  - add layout tests proving Stark carriers match C ABI layout on supported targets

- [ ] Add LZ4 frame error handling:
  - bind `LZ4F_isError` and `LZ4F_getErrorName`
  - create `LZ4FrameError` and `LZ4FrameResult` forms
  - convert all `size_t` frame function returns through `LZ4F_isError`
  - test native error conversion

- [ ] Add one-shot frame compression:
  - bind `LZ4F_compressFrame`, `LZ4F_compressFrameBound`, and `LZ4F_compressionLevel_max`
  - expose `CompressFrame(source, destination, preferences)` and `MaxFrameCompressedSize(sourceLength, preferences)`
  - test frame compression followed by frame decompression

- [ ] Add frame compression contexts:
  - bind `LZ4F_getVersion`, `LZ4F_createCompressionContext`, and `LZ4F_freeCompressionContext`
  - expose an owned `FrameCompressionContext`
  - test creation/free and repeated reuse

- [ ] Add streaming frame compression:
  - bind `LZ4F_compressBegin`, `LZ4F_compressBound`, `LZ4F_compressUpdate`, `LZ4F_flush`, and `LZ4F_compressEnd`
  - expose a safe streaming frame writer over caller-owned output buffers
  - test multi-chunk compression, explicit flush, and final end marker

- [ ] Add frame decompression contexts:
  - bind `LZ4F_createDecompressionContext`, `LZ4F_freeDecompressionContext`, and `LZ4F_resetDecompressionContext`
  - expose an owned `FrameDecompressionContext`
  - test reset after an error and reuse after a completed frame

- [ ] Add streaming frame decompression:
  - bind `LZ4F_headerSize`, `LZ4F_getFrameInfo`, and `LZ4F_decompress`
  - expose header inspection and incremental decompression with consumed/produced counts
  - test partial input, unconsumed tail handling, and frame info extraction

- [ ] Add frame dictionary APIs:
  - bind `LZ4F_compressBegin_usingDict`, `LZ4F_decompress_usingDict`, `LZ4F_createCDict`, `LZ4F_freeCDict`, `LZ4F_compressFrame_usingCDict`, and `LZ4F_compressBegin_usingCDict`
  - expose an owned read-only `FrameCompressionDictionary`
  - ensure dictionary input is copied or lifetime-pinned according to upstream semantics
  - test one-shot and streaming dictionary frame compression/decompression

- [ ] Update `examples/lz4/LZ4RoundTrip.stark`:
  - keep the current simple block example
  - add a frame round-trip path after frame APIs land
  - add a streaming dependent-block path after streaming APIs land
  - keep example output simple `WriteLine(...)` style

- [ ] Add C# compiler/integration tests for every new LZ4 surface:
  - source-check API shape
  - native package metadata
  - runtime round trips for block, HC, streaming, frame, and dictionary paths where the native library is available

- [ ] Add Stark self-hosted tests for every new LZ4 surface that the current Stark test harness can express:
  - source-level API shape tests
  - simple block/frame round trips
  - streaming state lifetime/drop tests

## `Vendor.Zlib`

### Source Of Truth

Audited against latest stable upstream zlib release `v1.3.2`, published
February 17, 2026:

- <https://www.zlib.net/>
- <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/madler/zlib/v1.3.2/zlib.h>
- <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/madler/zlib/v1.3.2/zconf.h>

Scope note: this audit covers the core zlib API declared by `zlib.h` and the
platform/typedef facts in `zconf.h`. The bundled `contrib/minizip` code is a
separate library surface and should be audited as `Vendor.Minizip` if Stark
decides to ship ZIP-file bindings.

### Current Stark Coverage

Current files:

- `vendor/src/Vendor/Zlib.stark`
- `vendor/ZlibStreamBinding.c`

Stark currently exposes:

- size constants `ZlibMaxNativeLength` and `ZlibMaxOneShotInputSize`
- compression level constants `ZLIB_NO_COMPRESSION`, `ZLIB_BEST_SPEED`,
  `ZLIB_BEST_COMPRESSION`, and `ZLIB_DEFAULT_COMPRESSION`
- flush constants `ZLIB_NO_FLUSH`, `ZLIB_SYNC_FLUSH`, and `ZLIB_FINISH`
- return constants `ZLIB_OK`, `ZLIB_STREAM_END`, `ZLIB_NEED_DICT`,
  `ZLIB_ERRNO`, `ZLIB_STREAM_ERROR`, `ZLIB_DATA_ERROR`, `ZLIB_MEM_ERROR`,
  `ZLIB_BUF_ERROR`, and `ZLIB_VERSION_ERROR`
- public enums/results `CompressionLevel`, `ZlibFlush`, `ZlibError`,
  `ZlibStatusResult`, `ZlibBlockResult`, `ZlibStreamStep`,
  `ZlibStreamStepResult`, `DeflateStreamResult`, and `InflateStreamResult`
- owned stream wrappers `DeflateStream` and `InflateStream`
- `IsOpen(stream)`
- one-shot helpers `MaxCompressedSize(sourceLength)`,
  `CompressBlock(source, destination, level)`, `DecompressBlock(compressed,
  destination)`, and `DecompressBlockPrefix(compressed, compressedLength,
  destination)`
- basic streaming helpers `StartDeflate(level)`, `StartInflate()`,
  `DeflateChunk(stream, source, sourceLength, destination, flush)`,
  `InflateChunk(stream, compressed, compressedLength, destination, flush)`,
  `CloseDeflate(stream)`, and `CloseInflate(stream)`

Current internal native symbols:

- direct zlib symbols `zlibVersion`, `compressBound`, `compress2`, and
  `uncompress`
- C adapter symbols `stark_zlib_deflate_init`,
  `stark_zlib_deflate_update`, `stark_zlib_deflate_dispose`,
  `stark_zlib_inflate_init`, `stark_zlib_inflate_update`, and
  `stark_zlib_inflate_dispose`

Assessment: `Vendor.Zlib` is incomplete. It supports one-shot zlib-wrapped
block compression/decompression and basic zlib-wrapped streaming. It does not
expose raw deflate mode, gzip-wrapped streaming mode, dictionaries, reset/reuse,
copy/tuning/header APIs, gzip file APIs, checksum helpers, compile/version
metadata as public Stark API, or the new `z_size_t` entry points from zlib
`v1.3.2`.

Performance note: the current streaming adapter heap-allocates a `z_stream`
wrapper for each `StartDeflate`/`StartInflate` and lacks reset APIs. That is
acceptable for a first safe binding, but high-throughput callers need reuse
paths (`deflateReset`, `inflateReset`, `deflateParams`, `deflateBound_z`) and
eventually caller-owned stream storage once Stark can model the `z_stream` C
layout and callback fields cleanly.

### Missing Stable Version And Compile Metadata API

- `zlibVersion`: native symbol is declared internally, but there is no public
  Stark wrapper.
- `zlibCompileFlags`: expose compile-time ABI/feature flags reported by the
  linked zlib.

Missing version constants/macros:

- `ZLIB_VERSION`
- `ZLIB_VERNUM`
- `ZLIB_VER_MAJOR`
- `ZLIB_VER_MINOR`
- `ZLIB_VER_REVISION`
- `ZLIB_VER_SUBREVISION`

### Missing Stable Constants, Modes, And ABI Carriers

Missing flush constants:

- `Z_PARTIAL_FLUSH`
- `Z_FULL_FLUSH`
- `Z_BLOCK`
- `Z_TREES`

Missing compression strategy constants:

- `Z_FILTERED`
- `Z_HUFFMAN_ONLY`
- `Z_RLE`
- `Z_FIXED`
- `Z_DEFAULT_STRATEGY`

Missing data-type/method constants:

- `Z_BINARY`
- `Z_TEXT`

- `Z_UNKNOWN`
- `Z_DEFLATED`

Missing public ABI carriers or safe wrappers for zlib C types:

- `Byte`

- `uLongf`

`Z_NULL` is also present upstream. Stark should document it as equivalent to
`null` rather than expose a redundant constant unless compatibility wrappers
need the spelling.

### Missing Stable One-Shot Compression API

- `compress`: default-level one-shot compression. Current `CompressBlock(...,
  CompressionLevel.Default)` is semantically equivalent, but the direct API
  shape is not exposed.
- `compress_z`: `z_size_t` one-shot compression added in zlib `v1.3.2`.
- `compress2_z`: `z_size_t` level-selected one-shot compression added in zlib
  `v1.3.2`.
- `compressBound_z`: `z_size_t` compression-bound helper added in zlib
  `v1.3.2`.
- `uncompress_z`: `z_size_t` one-shot decompression added in zlib `v1.3.2`.
- `uncompress2`: one-shot decompression that reports consumed source bytes.
- `uncompress2_z`: `z_size_t` `uncompress2` variant added in zlib `v1.3.2`.

`compress2`, `compressBound`, and `uncompress` are bound internally and covered
by current public wrappers.

### Missing Stable Deflate Streaming API

Basic `deflateInit`, `deflate`, and `deflateEnd` are covered indirectly by
`StartDeflate`, `DeflateChunk`, and `CloseDeflate`. The following stable
deflate APIs are still missing:

- `deflateInit2`: configure method, raw/zlib/gzip wrapper mode, window size,
  memory level, and strategy.
- `deflateSetDictionary`: set a preset compression dictionary.
- `deflateGetDictionary`: read back the active dictionary tail.
- `deflateCopy`: duplicate compression state.
- `deflateReset`: reset a stream for reuse.
- `deflateParams`: change level/strategy mid-stream.
- `deflateTune`: tune internal compression parameters.
- `deflateBound`: bound output for a specific initialized stream.
- `deflateBound_z`: `z_size_t` stream-specific bound added in zlib `v1.3.2`.
- `deflatePending`: report pending output bits/bytes.
- `deflateUsed`: report used bits in the last byte, added in zlib `v1.3.2`.
- `deflatePrime`: insert bits before compressed output.
- `deflateSetHeader`: provide gzip header metadata when using gzip mode.

### Missing Stable Inflate Streaming API

Basic `inflateInit`, `inflate`, and `inflateEnd` are covered indirectly by
`StartInflate`, `InflateChunk`, and `CloseInflate`. The following stable inflate
APIs are still missing:

- `inflateInit2`: configure raw/zlib/gzip wrapper mode and window size.
- `inflateSetDictionary`: provide a preset dictionary after `Z_NEED_DICT`.
- `inflateGetDictionary`: read back the active dictionary tail.
- `inflateSync`: resynchronize after corrupted input.
- `inflateCopy`: duplicate decompression state.
- `inflateReset`: reset a stream for reuse.
- `inflateReset2`: reset a stream and change wrapper/window mode.
- `inflatePrime`: insert bits before input.
- `inflateMark`: report the current inflate bit/byte location.
- `inflateGetHeader`: retrieve gzip header metadata when using gzip mode.
- `inflateBackInit`: initialize pull-style raw inflate.
- `inflateBack`: pull-style raw inflate with caller callbacks.
- `inflateBackEnd`: finish pull-style raw inflate.

### Missing Stable Gzip File API

The `gz*` family is completely missing. These APIs provide gzip file I/O over a
semi-opaque `gzFile` handle:

- `gzopen`
- `gzdopen`
- `gzbuffer`

- `gzeof`
- `gzdirect`
- `gzclose`

- `gzerror`
- `gzclearerr`

Missing stable large-file variants:

- `gzopen64`
- `gzseek64`
- `gztell64`
- `gzoffset64`

### Missing Stable Checksum API

- `adler32`

### Documented But Not Planned By Default

These symbols are present in the upstream headers, but they are compatibility,
private/undocumented, platform-specific, or awkward for Stark's safe public
surface. Keep them documented here, but do not expose them as ordinary safe APIs
unless a concrete compatibility need appears.

Version/sizeof init ABI behind C macros:

- `deflateInit_`
- `inflateInit_`
- `deflateInit2_`
- `inflateInit2_`
- `inflateBackInit_`

Stark should continue to route macro-style initialization through a small C
bridge or a generated ABI helper so `ZLIB_VERSION` and `sizeof(z_stream)` are
always correct for the linked headers.

Backward-compatibility/helper symbols:

- `gzgetc_`
- `gzopen_w`

Undocumented functions explicitly discouraged for ordinary applications:

## `Vendor.Curl`

### Source Of Truth

Audited against latest stable upstream curl/libcurl release `8.20.0`, published
April 29, 2026:

- <https://curl.se/>
- <https://curl.se/libcurl/c/allfuncs.html>
- <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/curl/curl/curl-8_20_0/include/curl/curl.h>
- <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/curl/curl/curl-8_20_0/include/curl/easy.h>
- <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/curl/curl/curl-8_20_0/include/curl/multi.h>
- <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/curl/curl/curl-8_20_0/include/curl/urlapi.h>
- <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/curl/curl/curl-8_20_0/include/curl/header.h>
- <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/curl/curl/curl-8_20_0/include/curl/websockets.h>
- <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/curl/curl/curl-8_20_0/include/curl/options.h>
- <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/curl/curl/curl-8_20_0/include/curl/mprintf.h>

Scope note: curl's live documentation can include symbols planned for a future
release. This audit pins the stable `curl-8_20_0` headers, so symbols that only
appear in later development documentation are intentionally excluded until the
next stable curl release is audited.

### Current Stark Coverage

Current files:

- `vendor/src/Vendor/Curl.stark`
- `vendor/CurlEasyBinding.c`

Stark currently exposes:

- `CurlMaxBufferLength`
- `CurlDefaultTimeoutMilliseconds`
- `CurlError`
- `CurlStatusResult`
- `CurlTransferInfo`
- `CurlTransferResult`
- `CurlResponse`
- `CurlResponseResult`
- `GetInto(url, bodyDestination, headerDestination, timeoutMilliseconds, followRedirects)`
- `GetBytes(url, timeoutMilliseconds, followRedirects)`

Current C adapter behavior:

- calls `curl_global_init(CURL_GLOBAL_DEFAULT)` lazily
- creates one easy handle per request with `curl_easy_init`
- sets `CURLOPT_URL`, `CURLOPT_HTTPGET`, `CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION`,
  `CURLOPT_MAXREDIRS`, `CURLOPT_TIMEOUT_MS`, `CURLOPT_NOSIGNAL`,
  `CURLOPT_ACCEPT_ENCODING`, `CURLOPT_USERAGENT`, `CURLOPT_WRITEFUNCTION`,
  `CURLOPT_WRITEDATA`, `CURLOPT_HEADERFUNCTION`, and `CURLOPT_HEADERDATA`
- calls `curl_easy_perform`
- reads `CURLINFO_RESPONSE_CODE`
- cleans the easy handle with `curl_easy_cleanup`
- stores body/header bytes either into caller-provided buffers or into a
  native heap response copied back into Stark dynamic storage

Assessment: `Vendor.Curl` is intentionally tiny and incomplete. It is a useful
HTTP GET convenience wrapper, not a libcurl binding. It does not expose easy
handles, typed `setopt` / `getinfo`, MIME uploads, headers, URL parsing, share
handles, multi/asynchronous transfers, WebSockets, slists, version/features,
TLS-session import/export, connect-only send/receive, custom callbacks, or the
majority of libcurl's enum/constant surface. It also hides global initialization
and never exposes cleanup, memory hooks, or SSL-backend selection.

Performance note: the current wrapper creates and destroys a fresh easy handle
for every request. That prevents connection reuse, DNS/cache reuse, HTTP/2 or
HTTP/3 multiplexing, shared cookies/DNS/TLS sessions, and user-controlled
buffer/callback strategy. A full binding should expose reusable easy and multi
handles first; the existing `GetInto` and `GetBytes` helpers can remain as
simple convenience APIs built on top.

### Tasks

- [ ] Add safe owned handle wrappers:
  - expose `EasyHandle`, `MultiHandle`, `ShareHandle`, `UrlHandle`, `Mime`, `MimePart`, `SList`, and deterministic close/drop patterns where applicable
  - bind `curl_easy_init`, `curl_easy_cleanup`, `curl_easy_duphandle`, `curl_easy_reset`, `curl_multi_init`, `curl_multi_cleanup`, `curl_share_init`, `curl_share_cleanup`, `curl_url`, and `curl_url_cleanup`
  - keep the existing `GetInto` / `GetBytes` helpers as convenience APIs implemented on the reusable handle layer

- [ ] Add typed `curl_easy_setopt` wrappers:
  - group options by ABI type (`long`, `curl_off_t`, string/CStr, blob, slist, handle/object pointer, function pointer, callback data)
  - expose stable enum-style option names for every non-deprecated `CURLOPT_*`
  - reject unsupported callback/value combinations at compile time where Stark type information can prove the mismatch
  - keep raw varargs use internal or behind tiny typed C adapters so Stark callers never pass an ABI-wrong value

- [ ] Add typed `curl_easy_getinfo` wrappers:
  - bind `curl_easy_getinfo`
  - expose separate helpers for string, long, double, `curl_off_t`, socket, slist, and pointer result families
  - cover every non-deprecated `CURLINFO_*`
  - keep `CURLINFO_RESPONSE_CODE` available as a cheap typed `ResponseCode(handle)` helper

- [ ] Add complete typed result/error enums:
  - cover `CURLcode`, `CURLMcode`, `CURLSHcode`, `CURLUcode`, `CURLHcode`, `CURLsslset`, and proxy `CURLPX_*`
  - bind `curl_easy_strerror`, `curl_multi_strerror`, `curl_share_strerror`, and `curl_url_strerror`
  - preserve numeric fallback variants for future libcurl values

- [ ] Add version and feature discovery:
  - bind `curl_version` and `curl_version_info`
  - expose `curl_version_info_data` through a safe copied Stark struct

## `Vendor.STB.Image`

### Source Of Truth

Audited against Stark's vendored STB snapshot:

- Upstream: <https://github.com/nothings/stb>
- Vendored commit: `31c1ad37456438565541f4919958214b6e762fb4`
- Vendored date: 2026-04-15
- Local headers:
  - `vendor/native/stb/stb_image.h` v2.30
  - `vendor/native/stb/stb_image_write.h` v1.16
  - `vendor/native/stb/stb_image_resize2.h` v2.18
- Current native implementation unit: `vendor/StbImageImplementation.c`

`StbImageImplementation.c` defines `STB_IMAGE_IMPLEMENTATION`,
`STB_IMAGE_WRITE_IMPLEMENTATION`, and `STB_IMAGE_RESIZE_IMPLEMENTATION`.
It does not define `STBI_NO_STDIO`, `STBI_WINDOWS_UTF8`,
`STBIW_WINDOWS_UTF8`, or `STBIR_PROFILE`, so stdio APIs are part of the
compiled surface, Windows wide-character conversion APIs are not compiled, and
resize profiling APIs are not compiled.

### Current Stark Coverage

Current file: `vendor/src/Vendor/STB/Image.stark`.

Stark currently exposes:

- `StbImageMaxNativeInputLength`
- `ImageChannels`
- `StbImageError`
- `StbImageStatus`
- `Image`
- `ImageResult`
- `LoadFromMemory(encoded, requestedChannels)`
- `LoadFromFile(filename, requestedChannels)`
- `WritePng(filename, image)`
- `WriteBmp(filename, image)`
- `WriteTga(filename, image)`
- `ResizeLinearInto(source, destination, outputWidth, outputHeight)`
- `ResizeLinear(source, outputWidth, outputHeight)`

Current internal native symbols:

- `stbi_load_from_memory`
- `stbi_load`
- `stbi_image_free`
- `stbi_write_png`
- `stbi_write_bmp`
- `stbi_write_tga`
- `stbir_resize_uint8_linear`

Assessment: `Vendor.STB.Image` is incomplete. The current binding is a useful
safe 8-bit image convenience layer, but it is not a full binding for the
vendored STB image stack. It omits most decode variants, image probes, load
controls, write targets/formats, writer controls, srgb and float resize paths,
medium-complexity resize controls, and the extended resize API that lets users
prebuild samplers and split a resize across threads.

### Covered By Stark Equivalents Or Internal Ownership

- `stbi_uc`: represented naturally as `u8`.
- `stbi_us`: represented naturally as `u16`.
- `STBI_default`, `STBI_grey`, `STBI_grey_alpha`, `STBI_rgb`,
  `STBI_rgb_alpha`: covered semantically by `ImageChannels`, though the native
  names are not exported.
- `stbi_image_free`: bound internally and used after copying STB-owned pixels
  into Stark-owned `dynamic` storage. This is appropriate for the current safe
  wrapper shape. If raw load APIs are added, a raw unsafe free surface or a
  Stark-owned native image handle will still be needed.
- `stbir_resize_uint8_linear`: bound internally, but only exposed through a
  packed `Image` wrapper using the source channel count as the pixel layout.
  A public full-argument wrapper is still missing for arbitrary strides and
  layouts.

### Missing Public Decode API From `stb_image.h`

- `STBI_VERSION`: expose the native header API version as a Stark constant.
- `stbi_io_callbacks`: expose the C callback carrier once callback ABI support
  is strong enough.
- `stbi_load_from_callbacks`: 8-bit decode from arbitrary callback input.
- `stbi_load_from_file`: 8-bit decode from an existing `FILE *`.
- `stbi_load_gif_from_memory`: animated GIF decode with frame count and per-frame delays.
- `stbi_load_16_from_memory`: 16-bit decode from memory.
- `stbi_load_16_from_callbacks`: 16-bit decode from callback input.
- `stbi_load_16`: 16-bit decode from filename.
- `stbi_load_from_file_16`: 16-bit decode from an existing `FILE *`.
- `stbi_loadf_from_memory`: float decode from memory.
- `stbi_loadf_from_callbacks`: float decode from callback input.
- `stbi_loadf`: float decode from filename.
- `stbi_loadf_from_file`: float decode from an existing `FILE *`.
- `stbi_hdr_to_ldr_gamma`: configure HDR-to-LDR gamma conversion.
- `stbi_hdr_to_ldr_scale`: configure HDR-to-LDR scale conversion.
- `stbi_ldr_to_hdr_gamma`: configure LDR-to-HDR gamma conversion.
- `stbi_ldr_to_hdr_scale`: configure LDR-to-HDR scale conversion.
- `stbi_is_hdr_from_callbacks`: query HDR status from callback input.
- `stbi_is_hdr_from_memory`: query HDR status from memory.
- `stbi_is_hdr`: query HDR status from filename.
- `stbi_is_hdr_from_file`: query HDR status from an existing `FILE *`.
- `stbi_failure_reason`: expose the most recent decode failure reason.
- `stbi_info_from_memory`: query width, height, and component count without decoding from memory.
- `stbi_info_from_callbacks`: query width, height, and component count without decoding from callback input.
- `stbi_info`: query width, height, and component count without decoding from filename.
- `stbi_info_from_file`: query width, height, and component count without decoding from an existing `FILE *`.
- `stbi_is_16_bit_from_memory`: query whether memory input is 16-bit.
- `stbi_is_16_bit_from_callbacks`: query whether callback input is 16-bit.
- `stbi_is_16_bit`: query whether filename input is 16-bit.
- `stbi_is_16_bit_from_file`: query whether `FILE *` input is 16-bit.
- `stbi_set_unpremultiply_on_load`: process premultiplied iPhone PNG alpha globally.
- `stbi_convert_iphone_png_to_rgb`: convert iPhone PNG BGRA data globally.
- `stbi_set_flip_vertically_on_load`: flip all decoded images globally.
- `stbi_set_unpremultiply_on_load_thread`: thread-local premultiplied alpha setting.
- `stbi_convert_iphone_png_to_rgb_thread`: thread-local iPhone PNG conversion setting.
- `stbi_set_flip_vertically_on_load_thread`: thread-local vertical flip setting.
- `stbi_zlib_decode_malloc_guesssize`: zlib decode to STB-allocated output.
- `stbi_zlib_decode_malloc_guesssize_headerflag`: zlib/no-header decode to STB-allocated output.
- `stbi_zlib_decode_malloc`: zlib decode to STB-allocated output.
- `stbi_zlib_decode_buffer`: zlib decode into caller storage.
- `stbi_zlib_decode_noheader_malloc`: raw deflate decode to STB-allocated output.
- `stbi_zlib_decode_noheader_buffer`: raw deflate decode into caller storage.

Conditional decode API not currently compiled:

- `stbi_convert_wchar_to_utf8`: requires defining `STBI_WINDOWS_UTF8`.

### Missing Public Write API From `stb_image_write.h`

- `stbi_write_tga_with_rle`: exported global writer setting for TGA RLE.
- `stbi_write_png_compression_level`: exported global writer setting for PNG compression level.
- `stbi_write_force_png_filter`: exported global writer setting for forced PNG filter mode.
- `stbi_write_hdr`: write float HDR image data to a filename.
- `stbi_write_jpg`: write 8-bit image data to a filename with quality control.
- `stbi_write_png_to_func`: write PNG bytes through a callback.
- `stbi_write_bmp_to_func`: write BMP bytes through a callback.
- `stbi_write_tga_to_func`: write TGA bytes through a callback.
- `stbi_write_hdr_to_func`: write HDR bytes through a callback.
- `stbi_write_jpg_to_func`: write JPG bytes through a callback.
- `stbi_flip_vertically_on_write`: global writer vertical flip setting.

Exported but less-prominent `stb_image_write.h` symbols also missing:

- `stbi_write_png_to_mem`: write PNG bytes to STB-allocated memory.
- `stbi_zlib_compress`: compress bytes with STB's writer zlib helper.

Conditional write API not currently compiled:

- `stbiw_convert_wchar_to_utf8`: requires defining `STBIW_WINDOWS_UTF8`.

### Binding Gaps That Need Design Attention

- Callback APIs need `ffi(c)` callback carriers or a tiny C bridge. Prefer direct
  Stark `fnptr<ffi(c)>` once callback ABI/lifetime tests are solid; use C shims
  only for real lifetime or calling-convention adaptation.
- `FILE *` APIs need an agreed C file-handle carrier, likely from `System.C`.
  They can be unsafe raw APIs first; safe file-path and memory APIs should stay
  the normal user-facing path.
- Writer configuration globals (`stbi_write_tga_with_rle`,
  `stbi_write_png_compression_level`, `stbi_write_force_png_filter`) need either
  direct FFI global-variable support or narrow native getter/setter shims. Direct
  FFI globals are preferable if the compiler supports them; accessors are an
  acceptable ABI bridge if it does not.
- 16-bit and float decode/write APIs should not be squeezed into the existing
  `Image` byte container. Add distinct `Image16` and `ImageF32`, or a generic
  image carrier only if Stark's current generic/layout support keeps it zero
  overhead.
- Extended resize state should be modeled as an ABI carrier with explicit
  lifetime rules. The performance win is sampler reuse and split execution; do
  not hide that behind an allocation-heavy wrapper.

## `Vendor.STB.Truetype`

### Source Of Truth

Audited against Stark's vendored STB snapshot:

- Upstream: <https://github.com/nothings/stb>
- Vendored commit: `31c1ad37456438565541f4919958214b6e762fb4`
- Vendored date: 2026-04-15
- Local header: `vendor/native/stb/stb_truetype.h` v1.26
- Current native implementation unit: `vendor/StbTruetypeImplementation.c`

The upstream `stb_truetype.h` header explicitly says it is not safe for
untrusted font files because it does not range-check all file offsets. That
does not block a vendor binding, but any Stark "safe" surface should either
state that the input font is trusted or add a validation layer before exposing
it as safe for arbitrary user data.

### Current Stark Coverage

Current file: `vendor/src/Vendor/STB/Truetype.stark`.

Stark currently exposes:

- `StbTrueTypeMaxNativeLength`
- `UnicodeMaxCodepoint`
- `GlyphId`
- `Font`
- `FontVerticalMetrics`
- `GlyphHorizontalMetrics`
- `GlyphBitmapBox`
- `PackedChar`
- `TrueTypeError`
- `TrueTypeStatus`
- `FontResult`
- `ScaleResult`
- `GlyphLookupResult`
- `FontVerticalMetricsResult`
- `GlyphHorizontalMetricsResult`
- `GlyphBitmapBoxResult`
- `LoadFontFromMemory(fontBytes, fontIndex)`
- `ScaleForPixelHeight(font, pixelHeight)`
- `FindGlyph(font, codepoint)`
- `GetVerticalMetrics(font)`
- `GetGlyphHorizontalMetrics(font, glyph)`
- `GetGlyphBitmapBox(font, glyph, scale)`
- `RenderGlyphBitmap(font, glyph, scale, destination, width, height, stride)`
- `PackGlyphRange(font, pixelHeight, firstCodepoint, glyphCount, atlasPixels, atlasWidth, atlasHeight, stride, padding, horizontalOversample, verticalOversample, packedChars)`

Current internal native symbols:

- `stark_stbtt_font_create`
- `stark_stbtt_font_destroy`
- `stark_stbtt_scale_for_pixel_height`
- `stark_stbtt_find_glyph`

- `stark_stbtt_get_glyph_bitmap_box`
- `stark_stbtt_make_glyph_bitmap`
- `stark_stbtt_pack_glyph_range`

The C wrapper internally uses:

- `stbtt_GetFontOffsetForIndex`
- `stbtt_InitFont`
- `stbtt_ScaleForPixelHeight`
- `stbtt_FindGlyphIndex`
- `stbtt_GetFontVMetrics`
- `stbtt_GetGlyphHMetrics`
- `stbtt_GetGlyphBitmapBox`
- `stbtt_MakeGlyphBitmap`
- `stbtt_PackBegin`
- `stbtt_PackSetOversampling`
- `stbtt_PackSetSkipMissingCodepoints`
- `stbtt_PackFontRange`
- `stbtt_PackEnd`

Assessment: `Vendor.STB.Truetype` is incomplete. It exposes a small safe
owned-font convenience API, but omits most of `stb_truetype.h`: texture baking,
raw/advanced packing, TTC font queries, EM scaling, OS/2 metrics, bounding
boxes, codepoint APIs, kerning, outlines, SVG glyph data, STB-allocated bitmap
helpers, subpixel/prefilter rendering, custom rasterization, SDF rendering,
font matching, and name-string access.

### Covered By Stark Equivalents Or Internal Ownership

- `stbtt_fontinfo`: wrapped inside the native-owned `Font` handle rather than
  exposed as a raw public ABI struct.
- `stbtt_packedchar`: represented by public `[StructLayout(C)]` `PackedChar`.
- `stbtt_FindGlyphIndex`: covered semantically by `FindGlyph`, except Stark
  maps glyph `0` to `MissingGlyph` instead of exposing the raw missing-glyph
  index.
- `stbtt_ScaleForPixelHeight`: covered by `ScaleForPixelHeight`.
- `stbtt_GetFontVMetrics`: covered by `GetVerticalMetrics`.
- `stbtt_GetGlyphHMetrics`: covered by `GetGlyphHorizontalMetrics`.
- `stbtt_GetGlyphBitmapBox`: covered only for equal `scale_x`/`scale_y` and
  no subpixel shift.
- `stbtt_MakeGlyphBitmap`: covered only for equal `scale_x`/`scale_y` and no
  subpixel shift.
- `stbtt_PackFontRange`: covered only by the one-shot `PackGlyphRange` helper.
  The public packing context, multiple ranges, point-size mode, gather/pack/render
  phases, and quad helpers are not exposed.

### Missing Texture Baking API

- `stbtt_bakedchar`: baked-character metric/texture coordinate carrier.
- `stbtt_aligned_quad`: quad carrier for baked/packed text rendering.
- `stbtt_BakeFontBitmap`: bake a continuous codepoint range with the older simple API.
- `stbtt_GetBakedQuad`: compute a render quad from `stbtt_bakedchar`.
- `stbtt_GetScaledFontVMetrics`: query scaled vertical metrics directly from font bytes.

### Missing Pack API

- `stbtt_pack_context`: explicit packing context carrier.
- `stbtt_pack_range`: multi-range packing descriptor.
- `stbrp_rect`: rectangle-pack carrier required by gather/pack/render APIs.
- `STBTT_POINT_SIZE(x)`: point-size marker helper.
- `stbtt_PackBegin`: initialize an explicit pack context.
- `stbtt_PackEnd`: end an explicit pack context and release its temporary storage.
- `stbtt_PackFontRange`: direct one-range pack API.
- `stbtt_PackFontRanges`: multi-range pack API.
- `stbtt_PackSetOversampling`: configure pack oversampling.
- `stbtt_PackSetSkipMissingCodepoints`: configure missing-codepoint handling.
- `stbtt_GetPackedQuad`: compute a render quad from `stbtt_packedchar`.
- `stbtt_PackFontRangesGatherRects`: gather packing rectangles for custom atlas packing.
- `stbtt_PackFontRangesPackRects`: pack previously gathered rectangles.
- `stbtt_PackFontRangesRenderIntoRects`: render gathered/packed rectangles.

### Missing Font Loading And Collection API

- `stbtt_GetNumberOfFonts`: count fonts in a TTF/TTC buffer.
- `stbtt_GetFontOffsetForIndex`: query a font offset by index.
- `stbtt_InitFont`: raw font-info initialization.

### Missing Character And Glyph Property API

- `stbtt_ScaleForMappingEmToPixels`: compute EM-to-pixel scale.
- `stbtt_GetFontVMetricsOS2`: query OS/2 typographic vertical metrics.
- `stbtt_GetFontBoundingBox`: query whole-font bounding box.
- `stbtt_GetCodepointHMetrics`: query horizontal metrics by Unicode codepoint.
- `stbtt_GetCodepointKernAdvance`: query kerning advance by Unicode codepoints.
- `stbtt_GetCodepointBox`: query glyph bounding box by Unicode codepoint.
- `stbtt_GetGlyphKernAdvance`: query kerning advance by glyph indices.
- `stbtt_GetGlyphBox`: query glyph bounding box by glyph index.
- `stbtt_kerningentry`: kerning table entry carrier.
- `stbtt_GetKerningTableLength`: query full kerning table length.
- `stbtt_GetKerningTable`: copy the full kerning table.

### Missing Glyph Shape And SVG API

- `STBTT_vmove`: glyph vertex move command constant.
- `STBTT_vline`: glyph vertex line command constant.
- `STBTT_vcurve`: glyph vertex quadratic curve command constant.

- `stbtt_GetGlyphSVG`: fetch SVG glyph data by glyph index.

### Missing Bitmap Rendering API

- `stbtt_FreeBitmap`: free bitmap storage returned by `stbtt_Get*Bitmap`.
- `stbtt_GetCodepointBitmap`: allocate and render a codepoint bitmap.

- `stbtt_MakeCodepointBitmap`: render a codepoint bitmap into caller storage.
- `stbtt_MakeCodepointBitmapSubpixel`: render a subpixel-shifted codepoint bitmap into caller storage.
- `stbtt_MakeCodepointBitmapSubpixelPrefilter`: render an oversampled/prefiltered codepoint bitmap.
- `stbtt_GetCodepointBitmapBox`: query codepoint bitmap bounds.
- `stbtt_GetCodepointBitmapBoxSubpixel`: query subpixel-shifted codepoint bitmap bounds.
- `stbtt_GetGlyphBitmap`: allocate and render a glyph bitmap.
- `stbtt_GetGlyphBitmapSubpixel`: allocate and render a subpixel-shifted glyph bitmap.
- `stbtt_MakeGlyphBitmapSubpixel`: render a subpixel-shifted glyph bitmap into caller storage.
- `stbtt_MakeGlyphBitmapSubpixelPrefilter`: render an oversampled/prefiltered glyph bitmap.
- `stbtt_GetGlyphBitmapBoxSubpixel`: query subpixel-shifted glyph bitmap bounds.
- `stbtt__bitmap`: raw rasterizer bitmap carrier.
- `stbtt_Rasterize`: rasterize caller-provided outline vertices into a bitmap.

### Missing Signed-Distance-Field API

- `stbtt_FreeSDF`: free SDF storage returned by SDF APIs.

### Compile-Time Configuration Not Exposed As Runtime API

- `STBTT_MAX_OVERSAMPLE`: compile-time upper bound for oversampling.
- `STBTT_RASTERIZER_VERSION`: compile-time old/new rasterizer selection.
- `STBTT_STATIC`: controls symbol visibility.
- `STBTT_malloc` / `STBTT_free`: allocator override hooks.
- `STBTT_ifloor` / `STBTT_iceil` / `STBTT_sqrt` / `STBTT_pow` /
  `STBTT_fmod` / `STBTT_cos` / `STBTT_acos` / `STBTT_fabs`: math override hooks.
- `STBTT_assert`, `STBTT_strlen`, `STBTT_memcpy`, `STBTT_memset`: runtime helper overrides.

These are documented here for completeness, but should not become ordinary
Stark APIs unless Stark needs build-profile variants of the native STB object.

### Binding Gaps That Need Design Attention

- The current safe wrapper copies font bytes into a native heap allocation and
  owns them for the lifetime of `Font`. That is safer than exposing STB's raw
  "caller keeps the byte buffer alive" contract, but it adds one copy at load
  time. Keep the safe wrapper; add raw/borrowed forms only if a benchmark shows
  the copy matters for large font collections.
- Directly exposing `stbtt_fontinfo`, `stbtt_pack_context`, and `stbrp_rect`
  requires exact ABI layout and lifetime rules. Prefer ABI carriers with
  `[StructLayout(C)]` where the header layout is public and stable; use opaque
  handles only when the native C side must own hidden allocation.
- STB-allocated outputs from shape, bitmap, and SDF APIs need deterministic
  ownership. Either copy into Stark-owned storage immediately or expose small
  native-owned handle types with `drop` calling the matching STB free function.
- Because upstream warns against untrusted font files, safe convenience APIs
  should be documented as trusted-input APIs unless Stark adds a separate
  validation pass.

## `Vendor.Miniaudio`

### Source Of Truth

Audited against latest stable upstream miniaudio release `0.11.25`, which
matches Stark's vendored snapshot:

- Upstream: <https://github.com/mackron/miniaudio>
- Documentation: <https://miniaud.io/docs/manual/index.html>
- Release: <https://github.com/mackron/miniaudio/releases/tag/0.11.25>
- Vendored commit: `9634bedb5b5a2ca38c1ee7108a9358a4e233f14d`
- Vendored date: 2026-03-03
- Local header: `vendor/native/miniaudio/miniaudio.h`
- Current native implementation unit: `vendor/MiniaudioImplementation.c`

The current native implementation defines these feature-removal macros before
including `miniaudio.h`:

- `MA_NO_ENCODING`
- `MA_NO_GENERATION`
- `MA_NO_RESOURCE_MANAGER`
- `MA_NO_NODE_GRAPH`
- `MA_NO_ENGINE`

That means the compiled `libVendorMiniaudio.a` intentionally omits encoding,
waveform/noise generation, resource management, node graph, and engine support.
The audit below still uses the full `0.11.25` public surface as source of
truth, because a complete vendor binding should either expose those families or
explicitly keep them unsupported.

The public function inventory was extracted from the pinned header with:

```bash
awk '
  /^MA_API / {
    line = $0
    sub(/\(.*/, "", line)
    n = split(line, parts, /[ *\t]+/)
    name = parts[n]
    if (name ~ /^(ma|ma_dr)_/) print name
  }
' vendor/native/miniaudio/miniaudio.h \
  | sort -u
```

This produces 1,190 unique public `MA_API` functions in `0.11.25`. The
family counts from that inventory are:

- core/log/allocation/thread/string/platform helpers: 95
- PCM conversion, channel maps, volume, resampling, and data converters: 151
- DSP/filtering/spatialization helpers: 240
- context/device/duplex device helpers: 36
- VFS helpers: 19
- data source helpers: 30
- audio buffer and paged audio buffer helpers: 41
- ring buffer and PCM ring buffer helpers: 38
- high-level decoding facade and built-in `ma_wav`/`ma_mp3`/`ma_flac`/`ma_stbvorbis` wrappers: 67
- embedded dr_wav API: 94
- embedded dr_flac API: 31
- embedded dr_mp3 API: 29
- encoder API: 10
- waveform/noise generation API: 19
- resource manager API: 64
- node graph API: 41
- engine API: 38
- sound and sound group API: 142
- miscellaneous backend/buffer-size/decoding-backend helpers: 6

- `ma_device_init`
- `ma_device_uninit`
- `ma_device_start`
- `ma_device_stop`

Assessment: `Vendor.Miniaudio` is incomplete. It is a safe convenience wrapper
for decoding to `f32`/`s16` and playing a complete `f32` sample buffer through a
default playback device. It does not expose miniaudio's low-level device/context
API, capture/duplex/loopback, device enumeration, callbacks, VFS, data-source
interface, conversion/resampling/filtering DSP, built-in encoder, generators,
audio/ring buffers, raw dr_wav/dr_flac/dr_mp3 APIs, resource manager, node graph,
engine, sounds, sound groups, spatialization controls, backend controls, or most
native result/format/backend constants and ABI carriers.

### Covered By Stark Equivalents Or Internal Ownership

- `ma_decoder_config_init`, `ma_decoder_init_memory`, `ma_decoder_init_file`,
  `ma_decoder_uninit`, `ma_decoder_get_data_format`,
  `ma_decoder_get_length_in_pcm_frames`, `ma_decoder_read_pcm_frames`, and
  `ma_decoder_seek_to_pcm_frame` are covered only through the current owned
  `Decoder` wrapper.
- `ma_device_config_init`, `ma_device_init`, `ma_device_uninit`,
  `ma_device_start`, and `ma_device_stop` are covered only through a restricted
  default playback wrapper that copies a complete `f32` sample buffer.
- `ma_format_f32` and `ma_format_s16` are covered by `SampleFormat.F32` and
  `SampleFormat.S16`. `ma_format_u8`, `ma_format_s24`, `ma_format_s32`, and
  `ma_format_unknown` are not exposed.
- `MA_MAX_CHANNELS` is enforced indirectly through the `u8[1 254]` public
  channel range, but the native constant is not exported.

### Binding Gaps That Need Design Attention

- Miniaudio's core model uses transparent structs whose addresses must remain
  stable for their lifetimes. Stark should use explicit ABI carriers and
  address-stable storage, or native-owned handles where the layout is too broad
  to make public safely.
- The current playback helper copies the entire sample buffer into a native
  allocation. That is safe, but it is not a substitute for low-latency
  callback-driven playback, capture, duplex, streaming, or ring-buffer APIs.
- Callback ABI is central to devices, VFS, data sources, custom backends,
  resource-manager jobs, node graphs, and sound end callbacks. Do not expose
  safe callback wrappers until lifetime, non-unwinding, and audio-thread
  restrictions are tested.
- Performance-sensitive APIs should preserve preallocated initialization,
  caller-owned heaps, direct slice processing, explicit channel maps, and
  zero-copy acquire/map operations. Avoid wrappers that allocate on every audio
  callback or hide format conversion in hot paths.
- Re-enabling `MA_NO_*` families changes the native object size and exported
  symbol set. The package metadata should record enabled miniaudio feature
  families, and tests should verify those symbols exist in `libVendorMiniaudio.a`.

## `Vendor.Cgltf`

### Source Of Truth

Audited against latest upstream cgltf release `v1.15`, which matches Stark's
vendored loader snapshot:

- Upstream: <https://github.com/jkuhlmann/cgltf>
- Releases: <https://github.com/jkuhlmann/cgltf/releases>
- Loader header: `vendor/native/cgltf/cgltf.h`
- Upstream writer header: <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jkuhlmann/cgltf/v1.15/cgltf_write.h>
- Vendored release: `v1.15`
- Vendored commit: `360db1a95480fe102ae9c69b27c5d101167ff5ba`
- Vendored date: 2025-02-09
- Current native implementation unit: `vendor/CgltfImplementation.c`

The upstream `v1.15` release is marked latest on GitHub and added
`cgltf_find_accessor`, sampler filter/wrap enums, `EXT_texture_webp`, and
`KHR_materials_diffuse_transmission`. Stark's vendor drop only includes
`cgltf.h`; upstream also ships `cgltf_write.h` with two public writer
functions. A complete cgltf vendor binding should either vendor and expose the
writer header or explicitly document that Stark's `Vendor.Cgltf` is loader-only.

The public loader function inventory was extracted from the pinned header with:

```bash
sed -n '843,904p' vendor/native/cgltf/cgltf.h \
  | rg 'cgltf_[A-Za-z0-9_]+\(' \
  | sed -E 's/.*(cgltf_[A-Za-z0-9_]+)\(.*/\1/' \
  | sort -u
```

This produces 37 public loader functions in `cgltf.h`. The public data-model
inventory contains 66 unique public `cgltf_*` enum/struct carriers.

### Current Stark Coverage

Current Stark file: `vendor/src/Vendor/Cgltf.stark`.

Current native file: `vendor/CgltfImplementation.c`.

Stark currently exposes:

- `Document`, an owning safe handle around an internal `stark_cgltf_document`
- `ParseFromMemory`
- `ParseFromFile`
- `Validate`
- `GetCounts`
- `GetMeshInfo`
- `GetMaterialInfo`
- `GetBufferInfo`
- `GetNodeInfo`
- `GetSceneInfo`
- `GetAnimationInfo`
- `GetAccessorInfo`
- `GetPrimitiveInfo`
- `CopyMeshNameBytes`
- `CopyMaterialNameBytes`
- `CopyBufferNameBytes`
- `CopyBufferUriBytes`
- `CopyNodeNameBytes`
- `CopySceneNameBytes`
- `CopyAnimationNameBytes`

The wrapper is useful for small asset-summary examples, but it is not a full
glTF binding. It does not expose the cgltf object graph, raw arrays, most
metadata fields, accessor payload reads, image/texture/sampler/skin/camera/light
details, extensions, extras JSON, material extension payloads, transform helpers,
custom file/memory callbacks, or writing.

### Complete Loader Function Inventory

- `cgltf_parse` - covered by `ParseFromMemory`, but raw options, zero-copy caller-owned lifetime, forced file type, token-count tuning, custom allocators, and custom file callbacks are missing.
- `cgltf_parse_file` - covered by `ParseFromFile`, but raw options, custom callbacks, and forced file type are missing.
- `cgltf_load_buffers` - partially covered only inside `ParseFromFile(..., LoadExternalBuffers, ...)`; there is no explicit post-parse load, no memory-parse buffer load, and no caller-controlled path.
- `cgltf_load_buffer_base64` - missing.
- `cgltf_decode_string` - missing.
- `cgltf_decode_uri` - missing.
- `cgltf_validate` - covered by `Validate`.
- `cgltf_free` - covered by `Document` drop, but raw ownership is not exposed.
- `cgltf_node_transform_local` - missing.

### Complete Writer Function Inventory

These functions are in upstream `cgltf_write.h`, but `cgltf_write.h` is not
vendored and no writer surface exists in Stark:

- `cgltf_write_file` - missing.
- `cgltf_write` - missing.

### Complete Public Type Inventory

Status values:

- `covered` means Stark exposes an equivalent safe value today.
- `partial` means Stark exposes only a small summary or a renamed subset.
- `missing` means there is no public Stark equivalent.

- `cgltf_accessor` - partial; `AccessorInfo` omits offset, min/max, sparse details, extras, extensions, and raw buffer access.
- `cgltf_accessor_sparse` - missing.
- `cgltf_alpha_mode` - partial; `AlphaMode` exposes opaque/mask/blend, but not exact native max enum.

- `cgltf_wrap_mode` - missing.

### Missing Data-Model Coverage

The most important gap is not just individual helper functions. cgltf is
designed as a transparent data graph, and Stark currently exposes only small
summary structs. Missing public data includes:

- root data: file type, asset metadata, default scene, variants, extensions
  used/required, unprocessed root extensions, extras, JSON chunk, BIN chunk,
  and custom memory/file callback state
- buffers and buffer views: buffer data pointer, data-free method, buffer-view
  offset/size/stride/type/data override, meshopt compression fields, extras,
  and extensions
- accessors: byte offset, min/max arrays, sparse count/index/value buffer views,
  sparse offsets/component types, extensions, extras, direct read helpers, and
  unpack helpers
- mesh primitives: attributes and attribute semantic/index pairs, morph targets,
  Draco compression, material variant mappings, extras, and extensions
- materials: full PBR metallic/roughness factors and textures, specular/glossiness,
  clearcoat, transmission, volume, IOR, specular, sheen, emissive strength,
  iridescence, diffuse transmission, anisotropy, dispersion, normal/occlusion/
  emissive texture views, alpha cutoff, emissive factor, extras, and extensions
- images/textures/samplers: image URI, buffer-view image data, MIME type,
  texture images including BasisU and WebP, sampler filter/wrap modes, extras,
  and extensions
- skins/cameras/lights: joints, skeleton, inverse bind matrices, perspective and
  orthographic camera parameters, punctual light type/color/intensity/range/spot
  cone fields, and extras/extensions
- nodes/scenes/animations: parent/child arrays, raw TRS/matrix values,
  mesh-gpu-instancing attributes, scene node arrays, animation samplers, channels,
  interpolation, target paths, and extras/extensions
- writer support: Stark cannot emit glTF JSON or GLB because `cgltf_write.h` is
  absent and there is no Stark-owned way to construct or expose a full `cgltf_data`
  graph

### Binding Gaps That Need Design Attention

- A complete binding should not copy vertex/index payloads unnecessarily. Accessor
  read/unpack helpers and buffer-view data should write into caller-owned buffers
  or expose borrow-scoped views tied to the owning `Document`.
- Exposing raw `cgltf_data` directly would require ABI carriers for many nested
  pointer-heavy structs. Safer high-level views can still be complete if every
  array item and helper has an index-based accessor that preserves document
  lifetime and avoids per-call heap allocation.
- `ParseFromMemory` currently copies the entire encoded input so cgltf's internal
  pointers stay valid. That is correct for safety, but a performance-complete
  binding should also expose a zero-copy parse path for caller-owned stable bytes
  whose lifetime is proven to outlive the `Document`.
- Custom `cgltf_options` matter for performance and integration: fixed file type,
  JSON token count, custom allocators, custom file callbacks, and controlled
  buffer loading all change allocations and I/O behavior.
- Writer support probably requires either a Stark-owned builder API for `cgltf_data`
  or a lower-level unsafe ABI layer. A safe writer that only serializes documents
  parsed by cgltf is useful, but it is not enough for asset-generation workflows.

## `Vendor.GLFW`

### Source Of Truth

Audited against upstream GLFW `3.4`, the latest GitHub release and the API version already hardcoded by `Vendor.GLFW` as `GlfwVersionMajor = 3`, `GlfwVersionMinor = 4`, `GlfwVersionRevision = 0`.

- Upstream: <https://github.com/glfw/glfw>
- Release: <https://github.com/glfw/glfw/releases/tag/3.4>
- Documentation: <https://www.glfw.org/docs/3.4/>
- Header used for inventory: <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/glfw/glfw/3.4/include/GLFW/glfw3.h>
- Native-access header: <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/glfw/glfw/3.4/include/GLFW/glfw3native.h>
- Local Stark binding: `vendor/src/Vendor/GLFW.stark`
- Local native callback bridge: `vendor/GlfwEventBridge.c`
- Build dependency: system `glfw3` package through `pkg-config` or explicit `GLFW_INCLUDE_DIR` / `GLFW_LIBRARY_DIR`

The current environment did not have `pkg-config glfw3` available when this audit was written, so the local installed-header version could not be checked. The audit is pinned to upstream `3.4` because that is the version declared by the Stark binding and the current GLFW latest release.

The public function inventory was extracted from `glfw3.h` with:

```bash
awk '/^GLFWAPI / { for (i=1;i<=NF;i++) if ($i ~ /^glfw[A-Za-z0-9_]+\(/) { sub(/\(.*/, "", $i); print $i; } }' glfw3.h | sort -u
```

This produces 124 public core `glfw*` functions. `glfw3native.h` adds 25
platform-native access functions, gated by `GLFW_EXPOSE_NATIVE_*` macros. The
public macro inventory contains 332 `GLFW_*` constants/macros. The public type
inventory contains 3 opaque handle types, 5 value/ABI structs, 2 generic
procedure typedefs, and 24 callback/allocator typedefs.

### Current Stark Coverage

Stark currently exposes safe ownership wrappers for:

- `Library`, initialized by `Initialize()` and terminated in `drop`
- `Window`, created by `CreateWindow` / `CreateHiddenWindow` and destroyed in `drop`
- version query, last-error enum mapping, default/window hints for a small hint subset, window size/framebuffer size, close flag, OpenGL context attach/detach, buffer swap/swap interval, time, key/mouse-button polling, cursor position, event polling/waiting, required Vulkan extension count/token, and Vulkan surface creation
- a fixed native event bridge for close, window size, framebuffer size, key, mouse button, cursor position, scroll, and focus events

The binding is useful for hidden windows, simple OpenGL/Vulkan bootstrap, and a fixed event queue. It is not a complete GLFW binding. It lacks monitors/video modes/gamma, fullscreen windows, window position/title/icon/opacity/attributes, cursor objects and cursor modes, clipboard, joystick/gamepad, most callbacks, custom allocators, init/platform selection, timer value/frequency, OpenGL extension/proc lookup, Vulkan proc/presentation helpers, user pointers, and most constants.

### Missing API Groups

- Initialization and platform selection: `glfwInitHint`, `glfwInitAllocator`, `glfwInitVulkanLoader`, `glfwGetVersionString`, `glfwSetErrorCallback`, `glfwGetPlatform`, and `glfwPlatformSupported` are missing.
- Monitors/video/gamma: every monitor enumeration, workarea, content-scale, physical-size, name, user-pointer, monitor-callback, video-mode, gamma, and gamma-ramp API is missing.
- Full window management: title get/set, icons, position, size limits, aspect ratio, frame size, content scale, opacity, iconify/restore/maximize/show/hide/focus/attention, fullscreen monitor reassignment, window attributes, and window user pointers are missing.
- Callbacks: Stark only exposes a fixed queued bridge for eight events. Raw callback setters and missing event kinds such as position, refresh, iconify, maximize, content scale, cursor enter, character input, file drop, monitor, joystick, and error callbacks are missing.
- Input/cursor: input modes, raw mouse motion, key names/scancodes, cursor setting, cursor objects, standard cursors, cursor position setting, clipboard, sticky keys/buttons, lock modifiers, and raw mouse motion constants are missing.
- Joystick/gamepad: every joystick/gamepad function, `GLFWgamepadstate`, joystick hats/buttons/axes constants, gamepad mapping update, and connection callback are missing.
- Context/proc lookup: `glfwExtensionSupported`, `glfwGetProcAddress`, timer value/frequency, and most context hints/constants are missing.
- Vulkan helpers: `glfwGetInstanceProcAddress` and `glfwGetPhysicalDevicePresentationSupport` are missing; required instance extensions are only exposed as a raw token and count.
- Native access: all `glfw3native.h` functions are missing, including Win32,
  Cocoa, X11, Wayland, WGL, NSGL, GLX, EGL, and OSMesa handles.
- Constants: most key codes, modifier masks, joystick/gamepad constants, framebuffer/context/window/input hints, cursor modes/shapes, platform constants, native context API constants, and init hints are missing from the public Stark surface.

### Binding Gaps That Need Design Attention

- GLFW has strict main-thread, callback, and pointer-lifetime rules. Safe Stark wrappers should encode or document main-thread-only usage and ensure callbacks cannot unwind into C.
- The current `GlfwEventBridge.c` uses one global fixed-size queue for all windows. That is simple, but a complete event model should support per-window queues or user data so high-rate input does not cause unrelated windows to drop events.
- The event bridge currently stores only integers and two doubles. Character input, file drop paths, monitor/joystick events, content scale, window position, and callback user data need lifetime-safe payload handling.
- Required Vulkan instance extensions should expose zero-copy indexed names or caller-owned copies, not just an opaque token. The token-only API is not enough to build a Vulkan instance in Stark without helper code.
- For performance, monitor/video-mode arrays, joystick axes/buttons/hats, gamepad state, and Vulkan extension names should expose borrowed views tied to GLFW lifetime, with optional caller-owned copy helpers where needed.
- Because GLFW is currently system-linked, tests should record the runtime/header version used by `pkg-config glfw3` and gate features that require exactly `3.4`.

## `Vendor.KbTextShape`

### Source Of Truth

`Vendor.KbTextShape` is not a direct binding to a single upstream library. It is a Stark-owned convenience wrapper over HarfBuzz for shaping and ICU BreakIterator/UText for Unicode segmentation. The audit therefore uses the upstream public APIs that the native bridge includes and links:

- HarfBuzz upstream: <https://github.com/harfbuzz/harfbuzz>
- HarfBuzz releases: <https://github.com/harfbuzz/harfbuzz/releases>
- HarfBuzz API docs: <https://harfbuzz.github.io/>
- ICU BreakIterator docs: <https://unicode-org.github.io/icu-docs/apidoc/released/icu4c/ubrk_8h.html>
- ICU UText docs: <https://unicode-org.github.io/icu-docs/apidoc/released/icu4c/utext_8h.html>
- Local Stark binding: `vendor/src/Vendor/KbTextShape.stark`
- Local native implementation unit: `vendor/KbTextShapeBinding.c`
- Build dependency: system `harfbuzz`, `icu-uc`, and `icu-i18n` packages through `pkg-config` or explicit include/library directories

The local development headers currently report HarfBuzz `14.2.1` and ICU `78.3`, matching the currently published upstream HarfBuzz release and ICU released API documentation. Because this package links system libraries instead of vendoring headers, the inventory should be regenerated whenever the supported system API version changes.

The HarfBuzz function inventory was extracted from installed public HarfBuzz headers with:

```bash
perl -0777 -ne 'while(/HB_EXTERN\s+([^;]+);/sg){ $d=$1; if($d =~ /\b(hb_[A-Za-z0-9_]+)\s*\(/){ print "$1\n" } }' /usr/include/harfbuzz/*.h | sort -u
```

The ICU segmentation inventory was extracted from `ubrk.h` and `utext.h` with:

```bash
perl -0777 -ne 'while(/(?:U_CAPI|U_DEPRECATED)\s+([^;]+);/sg){ $d=$1; if($d =~ /\b((?:ubrk|utext)_[A-Za-z0-9_]+)\s*\(/){ print "$1\n" } }' /usr/include/unicode/ubrk.h /usr/include/unicode/utext.h | sort -u
```

This produces 793 public HarfBuzz functions and 51 public ICU BreakIterator/UText functions. The current native bridge uses 20 HarfBuzz functions and 8 ICU functions internally, but exposes none of those raw APIs publicly.

### Current Stark Coverage

Stark currently exposes:

- `Segmenter`, an owning handle around an ICU `UBreakIterator`
- `Font`, an owning handle around HarfBuzz blob/face/font objects
- `CreateSegmenter(BreakKind)` for grapheme, word, and line segmentation only
- `CreateFontFromMemory(fontBytes, faceIndex)` with one copied in-memory font blob
- `UnitsPerEm`
- `SegmentUtf8Into` over Stark `ascii`, writing `TextBoundary` records into caller-owned output
- `ShapeUtf8Into` over Stark `ascii`, writing glyph id, cluster, advances, and offsets into caller-owned output

The current native bridge uses HarfBuzz with `hb_buffer_guess_segment_properties`, default OpenType font funcs, no explicit script/language/direction, no features, no variation coordinates, no font extents/metrics, no glyph names, no fallback fonts, no shaping plan reuse, no draw/paint/color/subset APIs, and no direct access to the HarfBuzz buffer. ICU usage is limited to `ubrk_open` with locale `und`, `utext_openUTF8`, forward iteration, and a single rule status per boundary.

### Missing API Groups

- HarfBuzz shaping controls: explicit direction, script, language, segment properties, feature ranges, variation selectors, shape plans, and shaper selection are missing.
- HarfBuzz buffer APIs: direct buffer ownership, Unicode/codepoint/UTF-16/UTF-32 input, output serialization/deserialization, normalization options, message callbacks, replacement codepoints, invisible glyph settings, glyph flags, cluster levels, and verification/diff APIs are missing.
- HarfBuzz blob/face/font APIs: file-backed blobs, sub-blobs, table access, face counts, table tags, glyph advances/origins/extents/names/contours, synthetic slant/bold, parent/sub-fonts, scale/ppem/ptem/variation coordinate access, custom font funcs, and user-data hooks are missing.
- OpenType APIs: layout scripts/languages/features/lookups, baselines, math, names, metrics, meta, variations, color palettes/layers/SVG/PNG/COLR paint, AAT layout, Graphite2 integration, and OpenType shape closures are missing.
- Rendering/extraction APIs: draw, paint, raster, vector, GPU paint/draw, glyph outlines, color glyph rendering, and image/raster surfaces are missing.
- Data structures/utilities: HarfBuzz set/map/common/tag/language/script/feature/variation parsing helpers, memory allocation wrappers, Unicode funcs, ICU/GLib/GObject/FreeType integrations, version checks, and subset APIs are missing.
- ICU BreakIterator APIs: sentence and title break types, locale-specific segmentation, custom rule strings, binary rules, clone/safe-clone, random-access navigation, current/previous/last/following/preceding/isBoundary, locale enumeration, full rule-status vectors, binary rule export, and refresh APIs are missing.
- ICU UText APIs: UTF-16 input, replaceable/character-iterator inputs, cloning, equality, random access, previous/next code point navigation, native index control, extraction, replacement/copy, writability/freezing, metadata, and custom UText provider setup are missing.
- Text model: Stark only accepts `ascii` even though the implementation calls UTF-8 APIs. There is no safe UTF-8/text type path for non-ASCII scripts, which is the primary reason to use HarfBuzz and ICU.

### Binding Gaps That Need Design Attention

- The current `ascii` parameter is too restrictive for a Unicode shaping package. A complete API needs a UTF-8 text type or a checked byte-slice entry point whose validity and lifetime are explicit.
- The current shape path creates and destroys an `hb_buffer_t` per call. That is safe, but high-throughput text layout should expose reusable buffer/shape-plan paths that avoid repeated allocation and shaper setup.
- `hb_buffer_pre_allocate(buffer, glyph_capacity)` makes zero-capacity count queries susceptible to allocation behavior. A count-query mode should either skip preallocation or use a reusable scratch buffer.
- `hb_buffer_guess_segment_properties` is convenient but not enough for production shaping. Script, direction, language, feature ranges, and variation coordinates need explicit Stark inputs so the compiler/user can name layout choices.
- Segmentation currently hardcodes locale `und` and exposes raw rule status as `i32`. A complete wrapper should expose locale, rule-status enums, and vectors without hidden allocations.
- A full HarfBuzz binding is much broader than text shaping. It may be better to split modules into `Vendor.HarfBuzz`, `Vendor.ICU.BreakIterator`, and a small `Vendor.KbTextShape` convenience layer built on top.

## `Vendor.SQLite`

### Source Of Truth

`Vendor.SQLite` is a Stark-owned safe wrapper over the SQLite C API. The current vendor package links the system `sqlite3` library through `pkg-config sqlite3` or explicit include/library directories; it does not vendor the SQLite amalgamation. The audit therefore uses SQLite `3.53.2`, matching both the current official SQLite download page and the local `pkg-config --modversion sqlite3` / `sqlite3 --version` result.

- Official download/version source: <https://www.sqlite.org/download.html>
- Official C interface function list: <https://www.sqlite.org/c3ref/funclist.html>
- Official complete C interface reference: <https://www.sqlite.org/capi3ref.html>
- Local public binding entrypoint: `vendor/src/Vendor/SQLite.stark`
- Local safe wrapper implementation: `vendor/src/Vendor/SQLite/Core.stark`
- Local public types/constants: `vendor/src/Vendor/SQLite/Types.stark`
- Local native helper: `vendor/SQLiteTextBinding.c`
- Build script: `vendor/build-sqlite-package.sh`

The official SQLite `3.53.2` C reference lists 304 public function entries, 495 constants, and 29 public object/type entries. The current Stark binding covers 27 official function names, 48 official constants, and 2 owning handles directly (`sqlite3` and `sqlite3_stmt`), with the integer typedefs represented by native Stark integer types rather than named aliases. The missing surface is 277 functions, 447 constants, and 23 object/table types.

The official function inventory was extracted from the SQLite function list with:

```bash
perl -ne 'while(/sqlite3_[A-Za-z0-9_]+/g){ print "$&\n" }' /tmp/sqlite-funclist.html | sort -u
```

The official object and constant inventories were extracted from the generated `capi3ref.html` index sections with:

```bash
awk '/<h2>List Of Objects/{flag=1;next}/<h2>List Of Constants/{flag=0}flag' capi3ref.html | perl -ne 'while(/\b(?:sqlite3|sqlite3_[A-Za-z0-9_]+|sqlite_[A-Za-z0-9_]+)\b/g){ print "$&\n" }' | sort -u
awk '/<h2>List Of Constants/{flag=1;next}/<h2>List Of Functions/{flag=0}flag' capi3ref.html | perl -ne 'while(/\bSQLITE_[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+\b/g){ print "$&\n" }' | sort -u
```

### Current Stark Coverage

The public Stark API currently exposes:

- owning `Database` and `Statement` structs that close/finalize in `drop`
- primary result/status and column-type enums
- primary result-code constants, basic column type constants, and a subset of `SQLITE_OPEN_*` flags
- library version/thread-safety helpers
- `Open`, `OpenReadOnly`, `OpenReadWrite`, `OpenReadWriteCreate`, and `OpenInMemory`
- `Close`, `Execute`, `Prepare`, `Finalize`, `Reset`, `ClearBindings`, and `Step`
- `BindNull`, `BindInt64`, `BindInt`, `BindDouble`, `BindText`, and `BindParameterIndex`
- `ColumnCount`, `ColumnType`, `ColumnInt64`, `ColumnInt`, `ColumnDouble`, `ColumnText`, and `ColumnName`
- `LastInsertRowId` and `Changes`

The native helper only exists to call `sqlite3_bind_text(..., SQLITE_TRANSIENT)` while hiding the destructor-function sentinel from Stark source.

### Missing API Groups

- Connection lifecycle and configuration: `sqlite3_open`, `sqlite3_open16`, close variants, extended result-code toggles, database config, file control, limits, db status, cache flush, readonly/name/filename helpers, transaction state, shared-cache controls, and autocommit introspection.
- Statement preparation and introspection: `sqlite3_prepare`, `sqlite3_prepare_v3`, all UTF-16 prepare variants, expanded/normalized SQL, readonly/busy/explain/scan-status/status APIs, parameter count/name APIs, and statement iteration.
- Binding and column value coverage: blob/blob64, text16/text64, zeroblob/zeroblob64, pointer/value binding, value accessors, column blob/bytes16/text16/value/origin/table/database/decltype APIs, and `sqlite3_data_count`.
- Incremental blob I/O: `sqlite3_blob` object and open/read/write/reopen/bytes/close APIs.
- Backup/snapshot/serialization: online backup object and functions, snapshot APIs, serialize/deserialize, WAL checkpoint and hook APIs.
- Custom SQL extension points: scalar/aggregate/window function registration, aggregate context, user data, aux data, result APIs, value APIs, collations, authorizer, overload function, auto-extension registration, load-extension controls, and `sqlite3_api_routines`.
- Hooks and callbacks: busy handler/timeout, progress handler, commit/rollback/update hooks, trace v2, preupdate hooks, unlock notify, log callback, autovacuum pages callback, clientdata, and custom error-message hooks.
- Virtual tables and VFS: `sqlite3_module`, `sqlite3_vtab`, `sqlite3_vtab_cursor`, `sqlite3_index_info`, vtab config/helper APIs, VFS registration/find/unregister, `sqlite3_file`, `sqlite3_io_methods`, file-name APIs, URI helpers, and database-file object access.
- Memory, mutex, and page-cache customization: global config, allocator APIs, memory stats/limits, mutex object/method APIs, pcache method/page types, release-memory APIs, and string-builder APIs.
- Introspection/utilities: compile options, keyword APIs, complete/complete16, randomness, sleep, system errno, table-column metadata, source ID, version variable, string compare/glob/like helpers, mprintf/snprintf families, and deprecated compatibility APIs.
- Constants: almost all extended result codes, config codes, db-config codes, file-control opcodes, IO capability flags, open flags, prepare flags, function flags, serialization flags, status/db-status/stmt-status codes, sync/locking/access/delete/version constants, authorizer action codes, trace flags, test controls, checkpoint modes, virtual-table constraint/operator flags, and Windows-specific constants are missing.

### Design Notes

- The existing safe API is useful and should stay; full coverage should be additive, likely split into safe convenience wrappers and a lower-level `Raw`/`C` submodule where the C API contract is necessarily exposed.
- Callback-heavy SQLite surfaces require first-class support for C callback function pointers or generated C trampolines. This affects custom functions, collations, hooks, virtual tables, VFS, memory/mutex/pcache methods, and extension entrypoints.
- Text is currently `ascii`/`OwnedAscii` even though SQLite text is byte-oriented UTF-8/UTF-16. Complete SQLite bindings need UTF-8-safe text and byte/blob paths without forcing callers through ASCII.
- The current `sqlite3_bind_text` helper is acceptable while Stark cannot spell `SQLITE_TRANSIENT` as a destructor sentinel directly. If Stark gains a safe way to model that sentinel, this helper can disappear.
- Performance-sensitive wrappers should avoid per-call allocations for hot statement loops, expose borrowed column slices where lifetime rules permit, and preserve SQLite zero-copy read paths behind explicit statement-step lifetime contracts.
