## `Vendor.SDL3`

### Source Of Truth

`Vendor.SDL3` is a Stark-owned safe wrapper over core SDL3. The current vendor package links the system `sdl3` library through `pkg-config sdl3` or explicit include/library directories, and includes only `<SDL3/SDL.h>` in `vendor/Sdl3Binding.c`.

- Official SDL3 public symbol index: <https://wiki.libsdl.org/SDL3/CategoryAPI>
- Official SDL releases: <https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/releases>
- Local SDL headers: `/usr/include/SDL3/SDL*.h`
- Local public binding: `vendor/src/Vendor/SDL3.stark`
- Local native bridge: `vendor/Sdl3Binding.c`
- Build script: `vendor/build-sdl3-package.sh`

The local development headers and library report SDL `3.4.10`, and the upstream releases page lists `3.4.10` as the latest stable release. The SDL wiki `CategoryAPI` page states that it is a list of every public symbol in SDL. For this audit, the generated public inventory is taken from that wiki index and cross-checked against the installed `3.4.10` headers. The wiki currently lists 1,321 functions, 1,329 macros, 137 datatypes, 124 structs, and 97 enum types. The installed headers expose 1,276 linkable `SDL_DECLSPEC`/`SDLMAIN_DECLSPEC` functions; 1,274 overlap with the wiki function list, 47 wiki-listed functions are inline/helper/future/extension-style symbols rather than linkable functions in these local headers, and 2 local runtime thread entrypoints are declared in the headers but not listed in the wiki function index.

The public symbol lists were extracted from the wiki with:

```bash
perl -0ne '
while(/<h2 class="anchorText" id="([^"]+)">.*?<!-- BEGIN CATEGORY LIST:.*?-->(.*?)<!-- END CATEGORY LIST -->/sg){
  my ($section,$body)=($1,$2);
  while($body =~ /<li><a href="[^"]+">([^<]+)<\/a><\/li>/g){ print "$section:$1\n"; }
}
' /tmp/sdl3-categoryapi.html
```

The local linkable function list was extracted from headers with:

```bash
perl -0777 -ne 'while(/(?:extern\s+)?(?:SDLMAIN_DECLSPEC|SDL_DECLSPEC)\s+[^;]*?\bSDLCALL\s+(SDL_[A-Za-z0-9_]+)\s*\(/sg){ print "$1\n" }' /usr/include/SDL3/SDL*.h | sort -u
```

### Current Stark Coverage

The public Stark API currently exposes:

- initialization owner `Library`, `Initialize`, `WasInitialized`, and `GetVersion`
- app metadata setting
- owning `Window`, `Renderer`, and `AudioStream` wrappers
- hidden/general window creation, show/hide, set/get size
- default/named renderer creation, draw color, clear, and present
- event pump, poll, wait-with-timeout, and push-quit helper
- a flattened `SdlEvent` record for selected window, keyboard, mouse, wheel, and audio-device events
- `AudioSpec`, default playback stream opening, byte put/get, available byte count, flush, clear, pause, resume, and paused query
- a small set of renamed Stark constants for init flags, window flags, key values, mouse buttons, audio formats, and default audio devices

The current native bridge calls 31 SDL functions. It exposes 6 SDL datatypes through safe owners or raw opaque carriers, partially/fully covers 2 structs, partially covers 2 enum types by hardcoded selected values, and covers 39 wiki-listed macros through renamed Stark constants or internal native use. It does not expose a raw SDL3 module with original SDL symbol names.

### Missing API Groups

- Core lifecycle and error handling: additional app-main callbacks, main/runtime entrypoints, assertion handling, clear/set/get error variants, log categories/priorities/output callbacks, hint callbacks, memory allocation hooks, version/revision macros, and platform detection helpers.
- Video/window/display: full display enumeration and modes, window creation properties, window positioning, sizing constraints, fullscreen modes, opacity, parent/modal relationships, hit testing, surfaces, screen saver, text input, clipboard/primary selection, cursor/mouse capture, EGL/OpenGL/Metal/Vulkan bridge APIs, native platform properties, and all related constants/types.
- Rendering/surfaces/textures/pixels: renderer enumeration/properties, texture creation/properties/update/lock, render geometry/lines/points/rects, render viewport/scale/target/logical presentation, surface creation/conversion/blit/fill/palette/color-key/RLE/alternate-image APIs, pixel format and colorspace helpers, blend modes, rectangles, and every carrier struct/enum.
- GPU: device creation, shader/pipeline/sampler/texture/buffer/transfer-buffer creation, command/copy/render/compute passes, swapchains, fences, uploads/downloads, indirect draw/dispatch, render-state APIs, Vulkan interop, and all GPU structs/enums/flags.
- Audio: device enumeration and formats, logical/physical device management, audio stream creation/binding/callbacks/gain/frequency/channel maps/properties, sample conversion, format helpers, driver enumeration, and complete audio constants/enums.
- Events/input: full `SDL_Event` union, all event kinds, event filters/watchers/state/flush/peep APIs, keyboard/scancode/keycode/mod/text-input APIs, mouse/cursor APIs, touch/pen, joystick, gamepad, virtual joystick/gamepad, sensors, haptics, HIDAPI, and all callback/ID/enum carriers.
- Filesystem/storage/IO/process/async I/O: path helpers, directory create/enumerate/copy/remove/rename, storage backends, IOStream construction/read/write/seek/printf helpers, async IO queues, process creation/properties/wait/IO, loadable shared objects, dialogs, and every callback carrier.
- Threading/synchronization/time: threads, TLS, main-thread callbacks, atomic operations, mutexes, RW locks, semaphores, conditions, timers, high-resolution time, date/time conversion, and all related callback/function-pointer types.
- Properties/environment/locale/system/power/misc: property containers, environment variables, locale preferences, power state, CPU/SIMD/system RAM/page-size queries, Android/iOS/GDK/Windows/X11 hooks, tray APIs, message boxes, and platform-specific native handles.
- Standard-library helpers: SDL memory/string/math/CRC/iconv/sort/search/endian/bits helpers that are public through SDL headers and wiki macros/functions.
- Raw ABI surface: most datatypes, structs, enums, and macros are not represented as Stark ABI carriers or named constants, even where the current safe wrapper uses selected hardcoded values.

### Design Notes

- Keep `Vendor.SDL3` as the safe ergonomic layer, but add a low-level raw namespace for complete SDL symbol coverage. This avoids forcing every SDL program through a high-level API while preserving the existing safe wrappers.
- Several SDL APIs require C callbacks or function-pointer tables: app callbacks, event filters/watchers, audio callbacks, timers, log output, hint callbacks, file dialogs, async IO callbacks, thread entrypoints, cleanup callbacks, tray callbacks, property cleanup callbacks, and platform hooks. These need first-class callback lowering or generated non-allocating C trampolines.
- The current flattened event bridge is useful for simple examples but loses most of `SDL_Event`. A complete binding needs either a full ABI carrier for the union or a generated tagged-safe representation covering every event payload.
- Strings are currently `ascii`; SDL uses UTF-8 for user-facing text. Complete bindings need safe UTF-8/byte-string support rather than expanding ASCII-only wrappers.
- Performance-sensitive paths should expose zero-copy views where SDL lifetime rules allow it, avoid per-call allocations in event/audio/render loops, preserve caller-owned buffers, and keep raw SDL calls direct enough for LLVM to inline wrapper logic around FFI boundaries.
- SDL_image, SDL_ttf, and other satellite libraries should be audited as separate vendor packages if they are added. This section is for core SDL3 plus the symbols visible through the SDL3 public symbol index and core headers.

## `Vendor.Raylib`

### Source Of Truth

Audited against official Raylib `6.0`, released April 23, 2026. The core binding is compared against `src/raylib.h`; the Raylib-distributed helper headers `src/raymath.h` and `src/rlgl.h` are exposed through sibling `Vendor.Raymath` and `Vendor.Rlgl` modules in the same Vendor package.

- <https://github.com/raysan5/raylib/blob/6.0/CHANGELOG>
- <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raysan5/raylib/6.0/src/raylib.h>
- <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raysan5/raylib/6.0/src/raymath.h>
- <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raysan5/raylib/6.0/src/rlgl.h>

### Current Stark Coverage

Current files: `vendor/src/Vendor/Raylib.stark`, `vendor/src/Vendor/Raylib/*.stark`, `vendor/src/Vendor/Raymath.stark`, and `vendor/src/Vendor/Rlgl.stark`.

Core `raylib.h` coverage:

- Functions: 600 of 600 official `RLAPI` functions are exposed.
- Structs: 35 of 35 public structs are exposed as Stark ABI carriers.
- Enum values: 303 of 303 public enum members are exposed as public constants.
- Named enum types: 0 of 22 upstream C enum type names are exposed as Stark enum types; the values are currently represented as integer constants.
- Callback typedefs: 6 of 6 callback names are present, but they are weak `rawptr<i8[min max]>` aliases rather than typed function-pointer carriers.
- Public macros: user-facing value macros are mostly covered through constants or zero-cost color constructor functions; C preprocessor configuration macros are not useful Stark APIs.

Related header coverage:

- `raymath.h`: 146 of 146 public helper functions are exposed in `Vendor.Raymath` as inline Stark `finite law` math where possible, avoiding FFI overhead and enabling caller-side LLVM optimization.
- `rlgl.h`: 163 of 163 native `rl*` entry points have exact internal `[LinkName]` FFI declarations in `Vendor.Rlgl`. Safe public wrappers are exposed for the 161 entry points that can be represented without leaking raw pointers; `rlLoadExtensions` and `rlGetProcAddress` remain internal-only until Stark has a typed procedure-loader/procedure-address carrier.

Assessment: `Vendor.Raylib` now covers the official Raylib 6.0 core function surface, removes stale non-6.0 model-point draw wrappers, exposes `raymath.h`, and exposes `rlgl.h` without public raw pointer APIs in the new module. It remains incomplete because callback aliases need real typed callback carriers, named enum types are not represented as strong Stark types, legacy public APIs still expose unsafe/raw surfaces, UTF-8/string ownership policy is incomplete, and many Raylib resource lifetimes still need safe owner wrappers.

### Core 6.0 Corrections

- `TextReplace`, `TextReplaceBetween`, and `TextInsert` allocate in Raylib 6.0 and are exposed as safe owned-text wrappers returning `RaylibTextResult` / `RaylibOwnedText`; the internal FFI edge uses the exact C symbol names and frees through Raylib `MemFree`.
- `DrawModelPoints` and `DrawModelPointsEx` were removed from the public 6.0 binding because they are not official Raylib 6.0 symbols.
- `GetMouseRay` remains exposed as a compatibility wrapper over `GetScreenToWorldRay`; this matches Raylib 6.0's macro compatibility alias and does not require a native symbol.

### Related `raymath.h` Coverage

`raymath.h` is exposed through `vendor/src/Vendor/Raymath.stark` as `module Vendor.Raymath`. All 146 extracted public helper functions are present. The implementation is intentionally Stark-side inline `finite law` math where possible instead of FFI, so vector, matrix, and quaternion helpers can inline into caller code and preserve optimizer visibility. Pointer-out C helpers are represented as safe value-returning carriers such as `Vector3Pair`, `QuaternionAxisAngle`, and `MatrixDecomposeResult`.

### Related `rlgl.h` Coverage

`rlgl.h` is exposed through `vendor/src/Vendor/Rlgl.stark` as `module Vendor.Rlgl`. All 163 extracted native `rl*` entry points have internal exact `[LinkName]` FFI declarations. The public surface exposes safe wrappers for the 161 upstream entry points that can be represented without leaking raw pointers, plus the Stark convenience wrapper `rlSetDefaultRenderBatchActive`.

`rlLoadExtensions` and `rlGetProcAddress` remain internal-only because a public wrapper would otherwise expose arbitrary raw loader/procedure pointers. Promote them only after Stark has a typed procedure-loader/procedure-address carrier that keeps raw pointers at the FFI edge.

### Missing API Groups

- Typed callbacks: file load/save, trace log, and audio callbacks should become typed Stark callback carriers once callback lowering can express the exact C signatures without heap trampolines in hot paths.
- Strong enum types: enum constants are present, but APIs still accept broad integer ranges. Strong Stark enum/flag types would catch mistakes without adding runtime cost.
- UTF-8 and owned text: many Raylib strings are UTF-8 `char *`; the binding mostly uses `ascii` or legacy raw-pointer APIs. Complete safe wrappers need a policy for UTF-8 borrowed strings, Raylib static buffers, and `MemFree`-owned returned text.
- Legacy public unsafe/raw surface: older core Raylib modules still expose raw pointers directly in several APIs. New bindings should keep raw pointers internal, and a cleanup pass should add safe wrappers or move raw-only APIs behind explicitly unsafe/internal edges.
- Resource ownership wrappers: raw resource structs are exposed, but complete safe owner types would prevent double-unload/missed-unload for `Image`, `Texture`, `RenderTexture`, `Font`, `Wave`, `Sound`, `Music`, `Model`, `Shader`, `Mesh`, and VR configs while preserving zero-cost pass-by-value ABI calls.
- Typed RLGL procedure loading: `rlLoadExtensions` and `rlGetProcAddress` are bound internally but intentionally not public until Stark can expose typed procedure-loader/procedure-address carriers without leaking arbitrary raw pointers.

### Design Notes

- Do not reintroduce C shim files for aggregate returns. The current FFI aggregate-carrier work should let `Vector2`, `Color`, `Image`, `Texture`, and other Raylib ABI structs pass and return directly.
- Keep hot draw/input/audio calls as direct wrappers over native symbols. Safe layers should be zero-allocation and inline-friendly; ownership checks should happen at construction/destruction boundaries, not per draw call.
- For alloc-returning text APIs, prefer an owning Stark type that records the `MemFree` obligation. Avoid returning a naked `rawmutptr<i8>` from the safe layer unless the API is explicitly marked unsafe/raw.
- Raylib named enum types are ABI `int` in C. Stark can expose strong enums or flag wrapper types while lowering parameters/results to `i32` with no ABI cost.
- `raymath.h` functions are mostly inline math helpers. Implementing them directly in Stark may outperform FFI because LLVM can inline and optimize them through caller code; only use native calls if the supported Raylib build exports external definitions.
- `rlgl.h` is lower-level than Raylib proper. Exposing it is useful for advanced renderers, but raw loader/procedure pointers still belong only at the unsafe FFI edge; public wrappers should use Stark slices, owner/result carriers, and value types.

- [ ] Add zero-cost strong enum/flag wrappers for Raylib enum families:

  - add C# integration tests for deterministic unload/drop behavior and Stark self-hosted tests for the owner APIs

- [ ] Clean up legacy public unsafe/raw Raylib APIs:
  - add safe slice/result/owner wrappers for raw-pointer data APIs without adding per-call heap allocation in hot draw/audio paths
  - keep direct raw FFI declarations internal where a safe wrapper fully covers the use case
  - document any intentionally unsafe advanced APIs and add C#/Stark source tests so raw pointers do not leak into ordinary safe examples

- [ ] Update Raylib examples and docs:

## `Vendor.Vulkan`

### Source Of Truth

Audited against official Khronos Vulkan-Headers tag `v1.4.354`, published June 12, 2026. The local binding is generated from `vendor/native/vulkan/vk.xml`, currently pinned to `vulkan-sdk-1.4.350.0` / header version `350`.

- <https://github.com/KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Headers/tags>
- <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Headers/v1.4.354/registry/vk.xml>
- <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Headers/v1.4.354/include/vulkan/vulkan_core.h>

### Current Stark Coverage

Current files: `vendor/src/Vendor/Vulkan.stark`, generated by `vendor/tools/generate-vulkan-binding.py` from `vendor/native/vulkan/vk.xml`, plus hand-authored support in `vendor/tools/vulkan-triangle-support.stark`.

- Registry version: local `VK_HEADER_VERSION = 350`, upstream `VK_HEADER_VERSION = 354`.
- Commands: 45 of 857 registry commands are bound as internal raw FFI; none are public raw `vk*` bindings.
- Handles: 59 public, 0 internal-only, 4 missing, out of 63.
- Structs: 2 public, 41 internal-only, 1692 missing, out of 1735.
- Unions: 0 public, 2 internal-only, 14 missing, out of 16.
- Basetypes: 6 public, 0 internal-only, 13 missing, out of 19.
- Bitmasks: 1 public, 31 internal-only, 238 missing, out of 270.
- Enum/flag scalar types: 2 public, 22 internal-only, 391 missing, out of 415.
- Define macros: 7 public, 0 internal-only, 16 missing, out of 23.
- Enum values/constants: 27 public, 64 internal-only, 6090 missing, out of 6181.
- Public convenience functions: 17; public result/helper enums: 9.

Assessment: `Vendor.Vulkan` is intentionally a minimal bootstrap and triangle-rendering helper, not a complete Vulkan binding. It can query the runtime, create a simple instance, count physical devices, create/destroy a platform surface token, and drive one fixed triangle path. It does not expose the full raw command surface, complete dispatch tables, device-level proc loading, most ABI carriers, pNext extension chains, allocation callbacks, synchronization/memory/pipeline/descriptors/rendering APIs, platform extension structs, video/raytracing/mesh/data-graph/tensor APIs, or the vast majority of constants.

Local input is `vulkan-sdk-1.4.350.0`; latest audited input is `v1.4.354`. New upstream registry entries since the local pin are listed here and also appear in the complete inventories below.

### Missing API Groups

- Registry freshness: the vendored `vk.xml` is four header drops behind the newest official Vulkan-Headers tag and misses new AMD GPA/session API entries plus related types/constants.
- Raw command surface: 812 registry commands have no Stark binding at all, and the 45 present commands are internal-only helpers rather than public raw `vk*` APIs.
- Dispatch: there is no generated global/instance/device dispatch layer for every command, no `vkGetDeviceProcAddr` path, no extension-aware availability table, and no fast preloaded device dispatch for hot paths.
- ABI carriers: most structs, unions, bitmasks, enum scalar types, aliases, and constants are absent or internal-only, so user code cannot build general Vulkan create-info chains or extension structs.
- pNext chains and extension typing: there is no safe/typed way to construct or validate `sType`/`pNext` extension chains across core and extension structs.
- Callbacks and allocators: `VkAllocationCallbacks`, debug callbacks, pipeline callbacks, validation callbacks, and other function-pointer surfaces are not first-class typed callback carriers.
- Platform surfaces: window-system/platform extension structs and commands are not generally represented; the current surface path accepts opaque surface tokens from GLFW-style helpers.
- Resource ownership: Vulkan handles are thin nullable wrappers, but there are no complete owner types tying destroy functions, parent handles, allocation callbacks, and lifetime ordering together.
- Safe layers: there are no safe wrappers for common workflows beyond instance/device count and the fixed triangle path: device selection, queues, memory, buffers, images, descriptors, command pools/buffers, sync, swapchains, dynamic rendering, compute, ray tracing, video, mesh shaders, timeline semaphores, or debug utils.

### Design Notes

- Generate the raw API from `vk.xml`; hand-maintaining Vulkan is not realistic. The generator should emit raw types, constants, commands, PFN aliases, and dispatch table slots deterministically from the registry.
- Keep performance central: resolve function pointers once into typed dispatch tables and call those directly. Do not perform string lookups or heap allocation in command-buffer recording, draw, dispatch, synchronization, or presentation hot paths.
- Treat public safe wrappers as a layer above the raw API. The raw layer should be complete and ABI-shaped; the safe layer should model ownership/lifetime and pNext correctness without hiding performance-critical choices.
- Vulkan structs are numerous but regular. `sType` defaults, pNext chain typing, array-count pairing, optional pointer/nullability, and parent-handle ownership can all be generated from registry metadata and validated by generated tests.
- Extension availability must remain explicit. Stark should make it easy to ask whether an extension command/type is available, but should not silently call unloaded device/instance extension functions.
